concepts.name: Buy-side / sell-side liquidity (old highs/lows)
concepts.definition: Resting buy stops plus breakout buys above an unswept swing high (BSL), and sell stops plus breakdown sells below an unswept swing low (SSL). A single old high suffices. Pool zone = [level, level + depth]. Swept when high > level (a strict trade-through; a wick is enough, no close needed).
concepts.dolRole: Defines the candidate set: the unswept obvious extremes are where order flow is drawn.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler RBS order data: stops cluster just beyond levels (stop-buys 14.4% at 01-10 above 00 vs 7.4% below). Kavajecz & Odders-White RFS 2004: S/R cointegrated with order-book depth peaks in 84% of series.
concepts.engineNotes: Chart pivots pivLen=5 (1753-1776). touched() strict >/< for liquidity (623-624). Zone depth 0.20 ATR (93).

concepts.name: Relative equal highs/lows (EQH/EQL)
concepts.definition: Two or more swing highs within a tolerance (ICT: 'close enough', 1-2 pips FX; practitioners 0.05-0.1% of price or 0.10-0.15 ATR) form one pool above the highest print.
concepts.dolRole: Marks the most obvious pools. ICT treats them as liquidity rather than resistance ('smooth edges like to be made jagged').
concepts.evidenceNotes: Distance-matched test, 8 markets, 2 years of 1H: EQ taken 63-82% vs ordinary swings 68-76% within 24 bars; the EQ label adds less than 1 pp beyond distance. Reversal after the sweep 39-44% for both.
concepts.engineNotes: eqTol 0.10 ATR (95). f_mergeAt moves the pool to the outermost print and increments eqCount (1111-1131). The density weight 0.9*eqCount (682) is large relative to the evidence.

concepts.name: EQH 'priming' (left high slightly above right)
concepts.definition: For a relative-equal pair, if the earlier high is slightly higher than the later one (lows: earlier slightly lower), ICT (2024 Mentorship L1, 1:15:22) calls a run on them 'very very high probability'.
concepts.dolRole: Would raise the draw priority of specific EQ pools.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ICT assertion only.
concepts.engineNotes: Could be flagged in f_mergeAt when a merged print is inside the stored price (not outer). Proposed as a feature bit in ICT-1.

concepts.name: STH/ITH/LTH swing hierarchy
concepts.definition: STH = 3-candle swing (lower high each side). ITH = STH with a lower STH on each side, or a high made rebalancing an imbalance. LTH = ITH with a lower ITH on each side, usually tied to the daily chart.
concepts.dolRole: Ranks pools by order: higher-order swings hold more stops and are the bigger draws.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ICT 2022 Mentorship Ep. 8 and Ep. 12 definitions.
concepts.engineNotes: Hierarchy is proxied by timeframe (chart/STF/HTF tier weights 0.25/0.45/0.65, f_tierW 506-516) and prominence. No nested pivots on the chart TF.

concepts.name: Key liquidity: PDH/PDL, PWH/PWL, Asia/London/NY highs and lows
concepts.definition: Previous calendar day/week extremes and session-range extremes, anchored to the printing candle. Swept on trade-through.
concepts.dolRole: Widely watched pools. Common daily DOLs and killzone raid targets (London raids Asia, NY raids London/PD).
concepts.evidenceNotes: YM: PDH break leads to a green session 67% (open-close) / 81% (close-close). SSRN 7359378: lower-high Friday raises Monday PDL-visit odds in all 6 markets, but the effect is small and absent in 2024-25 on index futures.
concepts.engineNotes: f_rangeTrack and f_sessTrack (807-863, 945-961). Registry push (1790-1809) and re-entry (1824-1852).

concepts.name: Stacked pools: outermost draw vs low-hanging fruit
concepts.definition: Same-side pools within a window form a stack. ICT trades to the 'lowest hanging fruit' (nearest stops) for partials and to the major/external pool for the full target.
concepts.dolRole: Chooses between the nearest pool (reached first) and the bigger objective behind it.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler: crossing a stop cluster accelerates price for hours, so the inner pool often carries price into the outer one. The ICT low-hanging-fruit rule itself is unvalidated.
concepts.engineNotes: f_stackSide (1230-1251). inner x0.70 (684-685). HTF objective ranked without proximity (1984-1989).

concepts.name: IRL/ERL delivery cycle
concepts.definition: Dealing range = swing low to swing high. ERL = stops beyond the range extremes. IRL = FVG/OB and short-term swing pools inside. After ERL is taken, price draws to IRL; after IRL is rebalanced, price draws to the next ERL.
concepts.dolRole: Decides whether the next draw is a retracement target (IRL) or an expansion target (ERL).
concepts.evidenceNotes: ICT 2022 Mentorship Ep. 3 (35:04), Ep. 4, Ep. 6 (45:49). No quantitative test found.
concepts.engineNotes: htfEQ/dayEQ are only confluence anchors (967-968, 1931). No range classification or phase state. Proposal ICT-4.

concepts.name: Premium/discount context
concepts.definition: pos = (close - rangeLow) / (rangeHigh - rangeLow). Premium if pos >= 0.5. ICT: a run below an old low while in discount is a turtle-soup buy; buy in discount and target premium ERL.
concepts.dolRole: Conditions reversal vs continuation after a sweep, and the IRL vs ERL preference.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ICT Core Content M1, Equilibrium vs Premium/Discount lectures.
concepts.engineNotes: Shown in the Terminal panel (2324-2333). Not used in D, scoring or the post-sweep read.

concepts.name: Sweep vs run (reversal vs continuation after liquidity is taken)
concepts.definition: Sweep = shallow trade-through that closes back inside and moves away (reversal). Run = closes beyond and holds (continuation). Codeable at bar close: HOLD if close >= level + 0.25 ATR; REJECT if close back inside; else NEUTRAL.
concepts.dolRole: Updates the draw direction after each raid. This is the core 'what happens next' signal.
concepts.evidenceNotes: SSRN 7430998: continuation in 65/66 walk-forward fold-selections. Distance-matched EQ test: reversal 39-44%. Osler: cascades for about 2 hours after crossing stop clusters. SSRN 7483658: sweep detectors 11-12 bp over 10 days, p >= 0.23.
concepts.engineNotes: Fixed rule at 1580-1582: close > zone top gives +1, close < level gives -1, times tier. The REJECT = reversal sign is unvalidated and probably miscalibrated. Proposal ICT-2.

concepts.name: Purge + market structure shift (MSS)
concepts.definition: After a sweep, a displacement body close through the last opposite short-term swing within N bars. ICT counts the MSS only after a purge, and the purge only if price moves away.
concepts.dolRole: Would confirm a reversal draw toward the opposite pool.
concepts.evidenceNotes: SSRN 7430998 found CHoCH+FVG reversal reads should be faded (negative evidence). ICT definitions only otherwise.
concepts.engineNotes: BOS/CHoCH (f_structure 708-782; bosUp/bosDn 1542-1547) are independent of sweeps. Folded into ICT-2 as a learned class.

concepts.name: Turtle soup (false breakout)
concepts.definition: Connors-Raschke: new 20-bar low, prior 20-bar low at least 4 bars old, entry 5-10 ticks back above the old low, stop 1 tick below today's low. ICT version: false break of an old high/low in premium/discount, followed by an aggressive response and an MSS.
concepts.dolRole: Reversal draw toward the opposite range extreme.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Original book claims only. Sweep studies (E6, E7) show continuation is more common.
concepts.engineNotes: Sweeps are read at 1580-1582 without a level-age requirement or premium/discount context.

concepts.name: Inducement (IDM, retail SMC)
concepts.definition: First pullback low after a BOS (follow lower lows until none). Taken on a wick. The POI behind it is valid only after the IDM is taken. Moves to the new break's first pullback if a new BOS comes first.
concepts.dolRole: The first liquidity met on the retrace in front of a POI (low-hanging fruit).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Community definitions disagree (pullback before vs after the break). Not an ICT term.
concepts.engineNotes: induceBar density feature (892-895) and inner pools (1230-1251). No IDM level. Not proposed (overlaps inner pools).

concepts.name: High- vs low-resistance liquidity runs
concepts.definition: A counter-trend run to an old high through lower highs and opposing PD arrays is high-resistance ('least probable'). A trend-direction run with a clear path is low-resistance ('hot knife through butter').
concepts.dolRole: Adjusts reachability by the structure in the path.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ICT Core Content M1 'Liquidity Runs' (7:26, 19:25).
concepts.engineNotes: Volume-profile path cost only (1945-1947). No count of opposing arrays in the path. Proposal ICT-5.

concepts.name: Trendline (phantom) liquidity
concepts.definition: Stops beyond an obvious diagonal with 3+ touches. Swept when price crosses line(t).
concepts.dolRole: Diagonal pool target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ICT: 'everybody's going to have a different diagonal trend line'; he prefers horizontal lines at EQH/EQL.
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended.

concepts.name: Tests / prior bounces at a level
concepts.definition: Approaches within a band that do not trade through. In the engine: within 0.30 ATR without taking, at least 3 bars apart.
concepts.dolRole: ICT/folk view: more stops accumulate. Empirical view: the next approach bounces more often in the short run.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Garzarelli et al. Sci Rep 2014: p(bounce | b_prev) > 0.5 and rising, p < 0.0001 at 45-90 s, not significant at 180 s. Chung & Bellotti 2021: same intraday; a 1-bounce level decays to 0.5 at about a 350-min window, a 4-bounce level at about 900 min.
concepts.engineNotes: track() (650-658) and density 0.35*min(tests,6) (682) reward tests as magnitude. The sign is questionable for a trade-through hit within H bars. Calibrate via ICT-1.

concepts.name: Stop depth beyond a level
concepts.definition: Stops are spread in a band beyond the level, not at one tick. Osler: stop-buys concentrate in the first 10% of the step above a round number.
concepts.dolRole: Sets zone depth, how 'spent' a shallow sweep is, and the invalidation buffer.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler SR125/SR150 Table I. Practitioner: stops just beyond the wick get re-swept; stops beyond the swing cost 1.5-2x the risk.
concepts.engineNotes: Fixed zoneATR 0.20 (93) and invalidation buffer 0.10 ATR (1344). Proposals ICT-3 and ICT-7.

concepts.name: Round-number stop and limit clusters
concepts.definition: Take-profit/limit orders cluster at 00/50 levels (bounce). Stop-losses cluster just beyond them (cascade after crossing). Auto step = 10^floor(log10(2 x daily ATR)); half step = step/2.
concepts.dolRole: Locates hidden stop pools and magnets near swing pools. Predicts acceleration after crossing.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler JF 2003: about 8.7% of orders at 00 vs 1% uniform; bounce +4.6 pp at round numbers. SR150 cascades significant for about 2 h. Lallouache-Abergel 2013: EBS order-book clustering at round prices.
concepts.engineNotes: No round-number logic anywhere (grep). Proposal ICT-3.

concepts.name: When a pool is spent
concepts.definition: ICT: once traded through, its orders are filled and the next untouched high/low becomes the target. In practice depth is graded: a 1-tick poke triggers only the nearest stops.
concepts.dolRole: Removes the target; triggers re-selection.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler stop distribution (band beyond levels).
concepts.engineNotes: Binary removal on trade-through (1583-1589); registry raid removal (1592-1596). Matches the decision history. Optional tagged state in ICT-7.

concepts.name: Killzone timing of raids
concepts.definition: London 2-5 am NY raids Asia; NY 7-10 am raids London/PD; avoid 12-1 pm; PM session from 1:30 pm.
concepts.dolRole: Timing and source affinity of the next raid.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor backtest: killzone-only sweeps 53.2% win rate / PF 1.68 vs 47.1% / 1.21 for 24 h (EURUSD, XAU H1, 2019-24).
concepts.engineNotes: f_kzAff (597-602) and off-killzone hysteresis (976). Fixed multipliers; calibrate via the ICT-1 KZ bit.

concepts.name: Daily bias from previous-range closes
concepts.definition: Bullish if C(t-1) > H(t-2), or if L(t-1) < L(t-2) and C(t-1) > L(t-2); draw = H(t-1). Bearish mirrors. Neutral otherwise. Same rule weekly.
concepts.dolRole: Picks the PDH vs PDL draw for the session and feeds the bias.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No independent backtest of the rule. Related: edgeful YM PDH-break continuation 67-81%; SSRN 7359378 small, regime-dependent lift.
concepts.engineNotes: D uses only MTF structure, displacement and liqEvt (1892-1894). Proposal ICT-6.

concepts.name: Top-down draw on liquidity (HTF first)
concepts.definition: Name the HTF draw (weekly/daily/4H): the unswept pool or unfilled imbalance in the direction of HTF delivery. Then trade the lower-TF legs toward it.
concepts.dolRole: Sets the draw side and the major objective.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ICT 2022 model; Ep. 14 ('start on the daily chart').
concepts.engineNotes: D vector sV = 0.5 htfBias + 0.3 stfBias + 0.2 exeIB (1892). Draw-side-first selection with hysteresis (1964-2035). HTF objective (1984-1989).

concepts.name: Level age / decay
concepts.definition: Liquidity matures as stops build, then goes stale. S/R memory decays with time since the last bounce.
concepts.dolRole: Freshness weighting of candidates.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Chung & Bellotti 2021 decay results (window-length and time-since-bounce).
concepts.engineNotes: Maturing-then-decaying freshness, half-life 4 x 150 bars (668-673).

concepts.name: Per-chart validation of ICT claims
concepts.definition: Grade every candidate level, not just the chosen DOL, against a distance-matched random-level baseline. Learn a lift per feature (EQ, tests, tier, session, killzone, round number, ERL/IRL, phase, daily-bias alignment, path resistance).
concepts.dolRole: Turns ICT heuristics into measured, bounded multipliers. Exposes the selection edge.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Standard distance-matched lift design (as in E6 and E11).
concepts.engineNotes: Ledger grades only the active DOL; f_calMult has 4 families (1376-1382, 1426-1499). Proposal ICT-1.

concepts.name: Liquidity voids, NWOG/NDOG, SMT divergence
concepts.definition: Multi-candle one-way voids; week/day opening gaps with a CE magnet; correlated-asset failure to take a pool.
concepts.dolRole: Additional draw sources and reversal tells.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ICT teaching; outside this domain.
concepts.engineNotes: Belongs to the PD-array / intermarket studies.

proposals.title: Candidate ledger with feature-level lift (validate every ICT claim on this chart)
proposals.rationale: The ledger grades only the active DOL (about one trial per H bars), so it can calibrate 4 families at most. Evidence shows ICT labels add little beyond distance on average (EQ under 1 pp; FVG about 5 pp) and vary by market. Grading all candidates against the existing distance-matched baseline lets the engine learn bounded lifts for EQ, tests, tier, inner, session, killzone, round number, ERL, phase, daily bias and path resistance. The trader sees which claims hold on this symbol plus a measurable selection edge. It is also the measurement backbone for ICT-2 to ICT-8.
proposals.spec:
Inputs (G_ACC):
- useFeat (bool, true)
- featN0 (int 40, shrinkage)
- featB (float 0.15, per-feature bound)

Types and state:
- New type Probe {int lvId, int side, bool liq, float edge, int bar0, float pBase, int mask}.
- Add int lastProbe = -100000 to Level.
- var array<Probe> probes, cap 256.
- NF = 14. var arrays fN, fK (int) and fE (float), size NF+1; index NF = all probes.

Feature mask (Pine has no bitwise operators: decode with int(math.floor(mask / math.pow(2, b))) % 2 == 1):
- 0 EQ (eqCount > 0); 1 PRIMED; 2 TESTED (tests >= 2); 3 INNER; 4 KEY (src >= 6); 5 SESSION (src 3-5); 6 MTF (src 1-2); 7 DRAW (side == dirSide); 8 KZ (f_kzAff > 1); 9 RN; 10 ERL; 11 PHASE; 12 DBIAS; 13 LOWRES.

Snapshot (step 17, after evaluate, inCalc and past warmup):
- For each pool level with bar_index - lastProbe >= H and 0 < dist/atr <= maxATR, push Probe(id, side, liq, nearEdge, bar_index, f_potBase(dist, side), mask).
- Set lastProbe := bar_index (one non-overlapping window per level).

Grading (step 2b, after the Trial loop at 1550-1557):
- hit = liq ? strict trade-through of edge : touch of edge.
- On hit, or after H bars, book: for each set bit and for NF: fN += 1, fK += y, fE += pBase. Remove the probe.

Lift and apply:
- lift_b = ((fK_b + 2) / (fE_b + 2)) / ((fK_NF + 2) / (fE_NF + 2)).
- w = n / (n + featN0); m_b = clamp(1 + w*(lift_b - 1), 1 - featB, 1 + featB).
- In the step 17 multiplier loop (1940-1947): lv.mult *= clamp(product of m_b over set bits, 0.75, 1.30).

UX (Terminal, Accuracy = Full):
- FEATURE LIFT rows with n.
- CANDIDATES hit % vs baseline.
- SELECTION EDGE = DOL lift / candidate lift.

Cost: at most 256 O(1) steps per bar.
proposals.risk: Probes on different levels share one price path, so variance is understated. Mitigate with shrinkage and bounds, or reuse the block-cluster variance from f_book. Feedback between lifts and pool membership: grade all candidates regardless of score. Adds a UDT and arrays; watch total memory and loop time on 20k-bar depth.

proposals.title: Post-sweep outcome learner (sweep vs run), purge+MSS event, honest sweep alert
proposals.rationale: liqEvt hard-codes close-back-inside = reversal and close-beyond = continuation (1580-1582). Multiple sources show continuation dominates after sweeps: SSRN 65/66 fold-selections; distance-matched reversal only 39-44%; PDH-break continuation 67-81%; Osler cascades for about 2 h. ICT conditions the read on premium/discount and a subsequent MSS. Learning P(continuation) per class and context, relative to the distance-implied race odds, fixes the draw vector's biggest unvalidated assumption. It also gives traders a measured readout and a purge alert.
proposals.spec:
Inputs (G_FLOW): swLearn (bool, true), swWin (int 8, MSS window), holdATR (float 0.25).

Type SweepRec {side, cls (0 HOLD, 1 REJECT, 2 NEUTRAL, 3 REJECT+MSS), ctx, lvl, cTgt, rTgt, mss, pModel, pen, bar0, tier}.
State: var array<SweepRec>, cap 64; var float arrays swN, swC, swP of size 8, indexed cls*2 + ctx.

Create at 1580 (hit and isLiquidity):
- cls: HOLD if close is beyond level by holdATR*atr; REJECT if close is back inside; else NEUTRAL.
- ctx = 1 if a BSL sweep happens at pos >= 0.5 of the STF range (stfRH/stfRL), or an SSL sweep at pos <= 0.5.
- cTgt = nearest same-side pool beyond the level, else level + side*1 ATR.
- rTgt = nearest opposite pool, else close - side*1 ATR.
- pModel = f_race(|cTgt - close|, |rTgt - close|, potSig, 0).
- mss = side == 1 ? nz(obSwingL, exeRL) : nz(obSwingH, exeRH).
- pen = penetration beyond the level in ATR.

Per bar (step 2c):
- Upgrade REJECT to cls 3 if, within swWin bars, a displacement body close crosses mss (dispDn/dispUp). This sets purgeEvt.
- Resolve the race with the f_step bar-path rule; expire after H bars without booking.
- Book swN, swC (continuations), swP (sum of pModel).

Use in D:
- pC = f_sigm(f_logit(pModel) + prior[cls] + dl), where dl = logit((C + 20 pbar) / (N + 20)) - logit(pbar) (same pattern as f_raceAdj).
- Priors (logit): HOLD +0.4, REJECT -0.2, NEUTRAL 0, REJECT+MSS -0.4.
- liqEvt := clamp(liqEvt + side*(2pC - 1)*tier, -1, 1). On an MSS upgrade, add the difference.

UX: Terminal row with per-class continuation/reversal % and n. Add P(cont) to the sweep alert. New alertcondition 'Liquidity Purge + MSS'.
proposals.risk: Sparse cells early on; priors and kappa = 20 handle the cold start. D could churn if liqEvt swings, so keep liqHL and the selection hysteresis. Target choice for cTgt/rTgt biases the race; the pModel normalization corrects for distance.

proposals.title: Round-number stop clusters: auto round step, confluence anchors, pool depth past round numbers
proposals.rationale: The strongest evidence in the domain (Osler JF 2003 and SR150; Lallouache-Abergel 2013) is that take-profits sit at round numbers (bounce +4.6 pp) and stop-losses sit just beyond them. Stop-buys are 14.4% at 01-10 above 00 vs 7.4% below, and crossings cascade for about 2 h. The engine has no round-number awareness. A swing high just under a round number has its real stop pool just above that number.
proposals.spec:
Inputs (G_LIQ): rnMode ('Off', 'Auto', 'Manual'), rnMan (float), rnDepth (bool, true).

Series (no request.security):
- atrD = nz(atrSlow) * sqrt(max(1, 86400 / chartS)).
- bool newDayRN = timeframe.change('D') at global scope. Never call it inside a v6 short-circuit condition.
- var float rnStep, recomputed when na or newDayRN: Manual ? rnMan : 10^floor(log10(max(2*atrD, 10*mintick))).
- Spot checks: EURUSD 0.01, USDJPY 1, ES 100, NQ 100, XAU 10, BTC 1000. Half step hs = rnStep/2.

Confluence: in step 17 anchors (1930-1933), push ceil/floor(close/hs)*hs and the same for rnStep.

Depth: where liquidity zones are built (1762, 1774, 1848), for BSL R = ceil(price/hs)*hs. If R - price <= 0.35 ATR, set top := min(price + 0.6 ATR, max(top, R + 0.10*hs)). SSL mirrors with floor. The hit rule (trade-through of price) is unchanged.

Add the RN feature bit for ICT-1.
proposals.risk: The auto step can be off by 10x on exotic symbols; use the Manual override. Zones become deeper, limited by the 0.6 ATR cap. Overlaps the confluence domain: coordinate so round numbers are not double counted.

proposals.title: IRL/ERL delivery-phase state plus dealing-range premium/discount
proposals.rationale: This is ICT's core rule for the next draw. After ERL is taken, price retraces to IRL inside the leg; after IRL is rebalanced, it expands to the next ERL. Buy in discount and target premium ERL. The engine has no range-relative classification or delivery memory, so it cannot tell a retracement draw from an expansion draw. Bounded and ledger-measured, it adds ICT's narrative without trusting it blindly.
proposals.spec:
Inputs (G_FLOW): drSrc ('HTF', 'STF', 'Execution'; default STF), kPhase (0.12), kPD (0.10).

State: var int phase (1 ERL taken, 2 IRL tagged), phaseSide, phaseBar; expires after H bars.

Classify with f_isERL(lv): liquidity with price >= rngH - 0.1 ATR (BSL) or <= rngL + 0.1 ATR (SSL). Everything else is IRL. rngH/rngL come from the chosen f_structure output.

Transitions in step 3:
- An ERL liquidity hit sets phase = 1 and phaseSide = side.
- An in-range array reaching fill >= 0.5 or hit sets phase = 2.

Multipliers in step 17:
- phase 1: IRL with side == -phaseSide x(1 + kPhase). ERL with side == phaseSide x(1 - kPhase/2), unless ICT-2 classed the sweep HOLD.
- phase 2: ERL with side == -phaseSide x(1 + kPhase).
- Premium/discount, pos = (close - rngL) / (rngH - rngL):
  - htfBias = 1 and pos < 0.5: BSL ERL x(1 + kPD*(0.5 - pos)*2);
  - htfBias = 1 and pos > 0.5: IRL arrays below x(1 + kPD*(pos - 0.5)*2);
  - mirror for bearish.

ERL and PHASE feature bits feed ICT-1.
UX: ERL/IRL tag in the HUD; Terminal 'DELIVERY' row.
proposals.risk: Overlaps the D vector (both encode trend), so keep k small and let ICT-1 calibrate. The dealing range from STF swings updates late; use the existing [1]-shifted confirmed values. No independent evidence, so it could add noise if not calibrated.

proposals.title: Structural path resistance (ICT high- vs low-resistance liquidity runs)
proposals.rationale: ICT calls a counter-trend run to an old high behind lower highs and opposing arrays the least probable condition, and a clear-path trend run a 'hot knife through butter'. The engine's path cost is volume-only. Counting unmitigated opposing PD arrays (and counter-trend swing pools) between price and target adds a structural reachability term that the ledger can test.
proposals.spec:
In step 17, before evaluate, for candidate lv (side s, near edge e):
- res = sum over pool arrays o of the opposing direction with side s (for a BSL target: kinds 3, 5, 7) whose near edge lies strictly between close and e.
- Weight each o by o.qual * (o.src == 2 ? 1.5 : 1).
- Add 0.5 for each same-side pool between price and e when htfBias == -s (lower highs in a downtrend).
- lv.mult *= clamp(1 / (1 + 0.12*res), 0.70, 1.0).
- Set the LOWRES bit (ICT-1) when res == 0 and dist > 1 ATR.

O(n^2) with n <= 40 (about 1,600 compares per inCalc bar). Pre-sorting near edges per side can speed it up.
proposals.risk: Double-penalizes counter-draw targets that already get ctrMult. Opposing arrays are also candidate targets, so circularity is possible. ICT-1 calibration of LOWRES limits harm.

proposals.title: ICT daily/weekly bias from previous-range closes (PDH/PDL rules) into D and key-level multipliers
proposals.rationale: The most common codeable ICT-derived daily bias is close above the prior high (or a swept prior low with a close back inside) means draw to PDH, and the mirror. The engine's D has no previous-range term. Related evidence: PDH/PDL breaks continue the session 62-81% on YM, and a lower-high leads to a modest next-day PDL-visit lift in 6 markets (regime-dependent). Cheap, non-repainting, and ledger-measurable.
proposals.spec:
At 956-961, inside if pdNew and before aPDH := pdH:
- c1 = close[1]. aPDH/aPDL still hold day t-2; pdH/pdL are day t-1.
- dBias := c1 > aPDH ? 1 : c1 < aPDL ? -1 : (pdL < aPDL and c1 > aPDL) ? 1 : (pdH > aPDH and c1 < aPDH) ? -1 : 0.
- Do the same with the W tracker for wBias.
- Confirmed history, so it does not repaint.

Use:
- sV += wDB * dBias, with input wDB default 0.15 (1892).
- Key-level multiplier: src == 6 and side == dBias x1.08; opposite x0.95.
- DBIAS feature bit (ICT-1).
- Terminal row 'DAY bias' (and week).
proposals.risk: A 24 h day vs a NY-session day changes results (edgeful uses the session only); consider an optional session mode. Regime decay (absent in 2024-25 on index futures in SSRN 7359378) is handled by calibration.

proposals.title: Learned stop depth: zone depth and invalidation buffer from observed sweep penetration
proposals.rationale: Stops sit in a band beyond levels (Osler), so 'how deep beyond a level stops sit' differs by symbol and timeframe. The engine uses fixed 0.20 ATR zones and a 0.10 ATR invalidation buffer. Learning the penetration distribution of rejected sweeps places zones where stops actually rest. It also puts the invalidation beyond the typical stop-hunt depth (fewer false invalidations, honest R:R).
proposals.spec:
From ICT-2, push pen (ATR) of each REJECT sweep into var array<float> penArr (cap 300).

When penArr.size() >= 30:
- q50 = penArr.percentile_linear_interpolation(50), q80 = ...(80).
- New pools use wPx = clamp(q50, 0.05, 0.6) * atr, replacing zoneATR in step 9/11 zone construction.
- f_invalidation uses buf = clamp(q80, 0.05, 0.8) * atr instead of 0.10 ATR (1344).
- Terminal: 'SWEEP DEPTH q50 / q80 ATR'.

Optional, off by default: pools swept by less than 0.5*q50 that close back inside stay as non-DOL-eligible context for H bars. The hit definition is unchanged.
proposals.risk: Only REJECT sweeps measure depth (HOLD runs are unbounded), which is a mild survivorship bias. Wider buffers lower displayed R:R. Changing zone depth alters zone visuals.

proposals.title: ICT swing hierarchy (STH to ITH to LTH) on the chart timeframe
proposals.rationale: ICT ranks old highs/lows by nested swing order (ITH = STH with lower STHs each side; LTH = ITH with lower ITHs each side). The engine proxies the hierarchy only by timeframe and uses pivLen 5 on the chart. Nested pivots add ICT's own ordering without extra requests, and can confirm ITHs earlier in fast legs.
proposals.spec:
- sth = ta.pivothigh(high, 1, 1), stl = ta.pivotlow(low, 1, 1), computed globally on every bar.
- Keep a 3-element ring of the latest STH prices and bars. When a new STH arrives and the middle one is above both neighbours, it is an ITH; push it to an ITH ring. When the middle ITH is above its neighbours, it is an LTH. Lows mirror.
- Create or merge chart pools at ITH/LTH prices via f_mergeLiq (1133); STHs never become pools.
- New Level field ord (2 = ITH, 3 = LTH). f_tierW gives chart ITH 0.30 and LTH 0.40.
- ITH/LTH feature bits for ICT-1.
- All state updates inside the confirmed-bar ENGINE block; pivot series computed globally.
proposals.risk: Duplicates and extra merges with pivLen pools (rely on the f_findLiq tolerance). Variable confirmation lag. More pool churn within the 40-level cap. No evidence; value depends on ICT-1 calibration.

result.summary: Five independent controlled backtests agree on one result: PD arrays are not magnets beyond distance. Price returns to FVGs and order blocks about as often as it returns to random zones of the same size at the same distance. FVGs: 73.0% vs 72.9% (Nordman, 38,114 returns). Order blocks: 73.7% vs 73.7% (10,986 touches). S&P daily bullish FVGs: 69% vs 69% within 20 days. BTC 1H FVGs: 75.6% vs 72.4%. SSRN Barot (about 40,000 FVGs): about 5 pp, no tradeable edge. The reaction at a zone is small (+2.5 to +5 pp) and lasts 5 to 15 minutes. Larger gaps and larger displacement fill LESS often in the near term: BTC daily large-tercile gaps fill 46% within 7 days vs 79% for small ones, and SPY gaps over 1% fill same-day 26 to 33% vs 78 to 80% for small gaps. So whether an array is reached within H bars is almost entirely a distance/volatility question. The engine's ledger already uses the right control (distance-matched random baseline). Its scoring has the wrong prior: arrays get a density bonus for displacement quality, gap size and HTF origin (line 687), which favors the arrays least likely to be revisited soon. The breaker logic is wrong. ICT's own wording ('Down Close Candle in the most recent Swing Low prior to an Old High being violated') requires the sweep by the leg LEAVING the block, but the engine filters on the block's own origin sweep (tookL/tookH, lines 1706/1747), ignores wick-raid breakers, and has no mitigation blocks. Premium/discount is display-only, and the strong literature (George and Hwang 2004) argues against hard-coding 'longs only in discount', so it should be learned through the ledger. ICT's own draw rule (liquidity first, arrays as waypoints, ERL/IRL alternation) is missing as target-type sequencing; it has no statistics but is measurable. Missing ICT level sources that need no request calls: IPDA 20/40/60-day extremes (canonical external range, where Donchian/Turtle stops cluster) and NWOG/NDOG opening gaps, whose size-dependent fill rates are documented. Old highs/lows have the strongest evidence of any array: Osler (2000) found published S/R levels bounce 60.8% vs 56.2% for random levels.

concepts.name: Dealing range, premium/discount, equilibrium
concepts.definition: Dealing range = the swing high and low of the most recent meaningful leg (one that swept liquidity or broke structure), usually on 4H/D. EQ = (H+L)/2. Premium is above EQ, discount below. Quadrants at 0.25/0.75; OTE at 0.62-0.79. Re-anchor when a close goes beyond either extreme.
concepts.dolRole: Side prior: from discount the draw is buy-side (premium arrays, BSL); from premium it is sell-side. Target ladder: EQ, then the opposite extreme.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics for the ICT rule. George & Hwang (2004, J. Finance) find nearness to the 52-week high predicts continuation (the opposite of 'sell premium') at monthly horizons in stocks. Intraday: no evidence either way.
concepts.engineNotes: f_structure keeps rngH/rngL (776-779). Terminal shows PREM/DISC % (2323-2336). dayEQ/htfEQ are confluence anchors (967-968, 1931). Not used in D, selection or the ledger.

concepts.name: PD array matrix ordering
concepts.definition: From the range extreme toward EQ: old high/low, rejection block, order block, FVG, liquidity void, breaker, mitigation block. Mirrored in discount. Later eras add VI, BPR, iFVG, NWOG/NDOG, propulsion and vacuum blocks.
concepts.dolRole: Ahead of price arrays are draws; behind price they are entry inventory. The ordering is spatial, not a strength ranking. For the draw, ICT ranks HTF pools above LTF, EQH/EQL above single swings, and untapped above probed.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Doctrine. The ordering varies across eras (LuxAlgo PD arrays page).
concepts.engineNotes: Liquidity has source tiers (f_tierW 505-516). Arrays use the same pillars with no type prior or waypoint logic (661-696).

concepts.name: Old high / old low
concepts.definition: A prior swing extreme with resting stops beyond it. Swept when price trades through.
concepts.dolRole: The primary DOL. Heads the premium/discount matrix.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler 2000 (FRBNY EPR): published S/R levels bounce 60.8% vs 56.2% for artificial levels (+4.0 to +5.6 pp by currency). Osler 2003 (J. Finance): stop-loss orders cluster beyond such levels, so trends accelerate after crossing.
concepts.engineNotes: Chart, STF and HTF pivots, PDH/PWH and sessions (1752-1853). Swept only when traded through (623-624).

concepts.name: Rejection block
concepts.definition: The body-to-wick span of a swing candle whose long wick ran liquidity: bearish = max(O,C) to the high, bullish = min(O,C) to the low. No fixed wick size; the wick must be conspicuous at a genuine swing.
concepts.dolRole: Refines where a target at an old high/low realistically completes. Practitioners trim take-profits to the wick zone's near edge.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: Pools extend beyond the swing by zoneATR (1762, 1774). The body extreme is not stored, so near-misses into the wick zone are invisible (proposal ICTPD-9).

concepts.name: Order block
concepts.definition: Bullish: the last down-close candle (ICT original: the largest-bodied down-close candle in the swing) before displacement that breaks structure. Validated when price trades above its high. Zone = full range (or body, or open-to-extreme). Mitigated = revisited; invalidated = body close beyond the far edge. Bearish mirrors.
concepts.dolRole: Entry zone on return to origin. As a target (an opposite-side OB ahead of price) it has reach probability equal to a random zone at the same distance.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Nordman 2026: price came back to 73.7% of OBs vs 73.7% of random zones (10,986 touches, ES/NQ/6E/6A 5m). Next-bar entry beats random by +4.8% at 1 min and +3.3% at 5 min. Fresh (20-bar) OBs are best. Size does not help.
concepts.engineNotes: 1663-1748. Created only on a body-close BOS. Takes the last down-close candle within 5 bars of the leg low (not the largest body; consecutive candles not merged). Quality = FVG in leg / origin sweep / leg size. Mitigated OBs are skipped.

concepts.name: Mean threshold
concepts.definition: 50% of an order block, measured over the range or the body (conventions differ). A body close beyond it is the first sign of failure; entries are preferred in the deeper half.
concepts.dolRole: Grades whether an OB is still valid. Its practical role is entry refinement.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A convention with no statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: Used only to skip already-mitigated OBs (1684, 1696-1700, 1727, 1737-1741).

concepts.name: Fair value gap (BISI/SIBI)
concepts.definition: Bullish: low[0] > high[2], zone [high[2], low[0]]. Bearish: high[0] < low[2], zone [high[0], low[2]]. Usually a minimum of 0.10-0.25 ATR and a displacement middle candle. The first presented FVG after an anchor (09:30 NY) ranks highest. Consecutive gaps can be joined.
concepts.dolRole: Internal range liquidity. A target when ahead of price (premium FVGs for longs); an entry when behind price.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Not a magnet. Revisits vs random: Nordman 73.0 vs 72.9% (38,114 returns); S&P daily bullish 69 vs 69% (20 days); BTC 1H 75.6 vs 72.4% (24 h); Barot SSRN about 5 pp with no tradeable edge. The reaction lasts 5-15 minutes.
concepts.engineNotes: 907-912 and 1867-1889. Size gate fvgMin plus quality gate fvgQMin. The origin lockout (689-690) treats a fresh FVG as an entry, not a target.

concepts.name: Array target quality (displacement / gap size as score)
concepts.definition: Using displacement strength, gap/leg size or HTF origin to raise an array's attractiveness as a TARGET.
concepts.dolRole: Should be neutral to negative for near-term reach: large displacement means continuation and slower refill.
concepts.evidenceNotes: BTC full fill within 7 days by size tercile, 1D: 78.7/61.7/46.0%. SPY opening gaps fill same-day 78-80% when 0.1-0.25% but 26-33% when over 1%. Nordman: gap size barely matters for reaction, and bigger OB gaps are not stronger.
concepts.engineNotes: Array density = 0.5*qual + ... + 0.20 for HTF (687). qual rises with body/ATR, gap size and leg size (912, 1870, 1880, 1692, 1735). The bonus is fine as a gate but wrong-signed as a target bonus (ICTPD-1).

concepts.name: Consequent encroachment
concepts.definition: The 50% line of an FVG (also applied to wicks, opening gaps and voids). Respected while closes hold on the near side of CE. A close through CE shifts expectation toward a full fill.
concepts.dolRole: Defines partial vs full delivery of an array target, and is a reaction level.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics for CE as a reaction level. The fill ladder exists: BTC 1H within 24 h is touch 85.3 / CE 80.6 / full 75.6%; 4H is 71.8/62.3/54.2%.
concepts.engineNotes: Non-active arrays are delivered at CE by default (123-124, 306, 1565-1577). The array target's glow line sits at the CE price. No CE/full probability readout (ICTPD-3).

concepts.name: FVG behavior: filled / respected / disrespected
concepts.definition: Filled = traded through the far edge. Respected = traded into (often only to CE) and continued in the gap's direction. Disrespected = a body close beyond the far edge, which becomes an iFVG. Breakaway gaps are not expected to fill; an immediate rebalance on the next candle is continuation.
concepts.dolRole: Respect implies continuation away from the array toward the opposite liquidity. Disrespect implies the draw continues through it.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No audited statistics for the labels. BTC: after the first touch, bullish FVGs go up 53.0% vs a 51.1% baseline; bearish FVGs are a coin flip.
concepts.engineNotes: Disrespect is detected as inversion (1598-1627). Respect is not tracked, and neither event feeds D.

concepts.name: Inversion FVG
concepts.definition: A candle body closes beyond the far edge of an FVG (some use beyond CE). The span then acts with opposite polarity until it is reclaimed.
concepts.dolRole: An entry/retest zone and a bias-flip cue, not a target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: One controlled test: S&P daily broken bullish gaps held as resistance on 38% of retests vs 38% for random zones; bearish 47% vs 47% (2014-2026: 50% vs 43-49%). No edge.
concepts.engineNotes: 1598-1644. Body close beyond the far edge; removed on failure or after more than ifvgMaxIn closes inside. Display and alert only, which is consistent with the evidence. Honest stats are proposal ICTPD-8.

concepts.name: Liquidity void
concepts.definition: A multi-candle one-directional run with porous price action, practically a stack of consecutive same-direction FVGs. Expected to be refilled later. Implement by joining consecutive FVGs (highest top, lowest bottom).
concepts.dolRole: An internal target after an external raid. A thin path speeds the run toward liquidity.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: The VP path cost and LVNs capture thin price (1945-1947). Consecutive FVGs stay separate levels (ICTPD-10).

concepts.name: Vacuum block / opening gaps (NWOG, NDOG)
concepts.definition: A true price gap from an event or a session break. NWOG = Friday close to the Sunday reopen; keep the last 5 with high, low and CE. NDOG = the CME 17:00 close to the 18:00 reopen; keep the last few. On RTH charts, the overnight gap. Crypto has none.
concepts.dolRole: A rebalance target (CE or full fill), and S/R at the edges and CE. Clusters of overlapping NWOGs are a stronger draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: SPY since 1993, same-day fill by gap size: up-gaps 78/60/46/26/27% and down-gaps 80/66/43/33/29% (0.1-0.25%, 0.25-0.5%, 0.5-1%, 1-2%, 2%+). Over 1% is gap-and-go (60% up days). NWOG/NDOG specifically: no audited statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: No session-break gap detection. Session opens are only confluence anchors (964-966). See ICTPD-6.

concepts.name: Volume imbalance
concepts.definition: Two consecutive candles whose bodies do not overlap while their wicks do (bullish: open[0] > close[1]). If the wicks do not overlap either, it is an opening gap.
concepts.dolRole: A micro reference that refines entries at an OB/FVG edge.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: Low value for DOL; not proposed.

concepts.name: Balanced price range (BPR)
concepts.definition: The intersection of a bullish FVG and a later bearish FVG over the same prices, or the reverse. The newer displacement sets the bias. Marked with high, low and midpoint.
concepts.dolRole: An entry zone only. 'Fill is the wrong frame.'
concepts.evidenceNotes: No audited statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: Low value for DOL; not proposed.

concepts.name: Breaker block
concepts.definition: Bearish: the down-close candle(s) at swing low L1 prior to an old high being violated (by wick or close), then a close below L1. Bullish: the up-close candle at swing high H1 prior to an old low being violated, then a close above H1. The qualifying sweep is made by the leg leaving the block.
concepts.dolRole: A retest/entry zone in the new direction, and evidence of control. As a target, a retracement destination.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics. Definition from ICT original text (studocu transcriptions) and LuxAlgo.
concepts.engineNotes: 1646-1661, 1706-1707, 1747-1748. Tracks only OBs whose own origin swept a 20-bar extreme (tookL/tookH, 1691/1734), which is the wrong side. Wick-raid breakers are missed because OBs need a body-close BOS (ICTPD-2).

concepts.name: Mitigation block
concepts.definition: The same role-flip as a breaker but without the sweep: the failing swing falls short of the prior extreme (a lower high), then structure breaks. Mark the block that launched the failed swing; conventions differ.
concepts.dolRole: A retest/entry zone, graded below a breaker.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: Failure swings are not tracked. Optional part of ICTPD-2.

concepts.name: Propulsion block
concepts.definition: A candle that trades into a prior OB (often to its MT) without closing through it, then launches away. It becomes a tighter continuation block.
concepts.dolRole: A continuation entry. Little target value.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: Not proposed (entry-only).

concepts.name: Implied FVG
concepts.definition: UWM = (H + max(O,C))/2, LWM = (min(O,C) + L)/2. Bullish if LWM_t > UWM_(t-2) and L_t <= H_(t-2); zone [UWM_(t-2), LWM_t].
concepts.dolRole: Secondary confluence when a displacement leg left no clean gap.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics; loosely specified.
concepts.engineNotes: Not proposed.

concepts.name: HTF arrays as magnets / IPDA data ranges
concepts.definition: HTF (daily/4H) FVGs and OBs define where price is going, and LTF arrays refine the entry. IPDA ranges = the 20/40/60-trading-day highest high and lowest low, framing the short, intermediate and long-term dealing ranges.
concepts.dolRole: HTF targets and external range liquidity. The 20/40/60-day extremes are where breakout stops cluster.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Daily S&P bullish FVGs are reached as often as random (69 vs 69%). Bearish ones beat random by 9 pp, likely the index's post-selloff bounce. IPDA has no statistics. Donchian/Turtle 20/55-day rules suggest order clustering. A one-year ES/NQ test found 20-session breaks often failed.
concepts.engineNotes: HTF FVGs only (785-796, 939-942, 1854-1865), +0.20 density and slower decay. No HTF OB. No 20/40/60-day extremes (ICTPD-5).

concepts.name: Internal vs external range liquidity alternation
concepts.definition: ERL = stops beyond the range extremes; IRL = FVGs/OBs inside the range. After ERL is taken (with rejection), the next draw is IRL. After IRL is rebalanced and price departs, the next draw is the opposite ERL. A genuine breakout breaks the rule.
concepts.dolRole: Decides the target TYPE next: a pool vs an array.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Doctrine only; no statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: Raid hold/reject feeds the direction D (1580-1582, 1892-1894), but there is no target-type sequencing (ICTPD-4).

concepts.name: Low- vs high-resistance liquidity runs
concepts.definition: A path through already-swept swings and same-direction FVGs is low resistance (fast). A path through fresh unswept swings and opposing imbalances is high resistance (slow, deep retracements).
concepts.dolRole: Probability and timing of reaching a pool.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler's +4.6 pp S/R excess bounce suggests a small per-level drag; array reactions last only about 15 minutes.
concepts.engineNotes: Inner stacked pools x0.70 (684-685) and the VP path cost (1945-1947). Opposing arrays in the path are ignored.

concepts.name: Displacement / MSS validation
concepts.definition: Arrays count only if the move away displaced: big-bodied candle(s) closing near their extremes, often leaving an FVG, and breaking a swing.
concepts.dolRole: A quality gate for arrays and a structure signal for bias.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Nordman 15,817 MSS signals: edge ratios about 1.0 with or without displacement. AMD study (arXiv 2610.35887): no information beyond the daily trend regime (aligned 62-71% correct, against 25-30%).
concepts.engineNotes: dispUp/dispDn (897-904); OBs require a BOS (1666-1681); FVG quality includes BOS proximity (1869-1870). Fine as a gate.

proposals.title: Evidence-based array target model: neutral density, large-displacement penalty, array prior, family edge vs expected
proposals.rationale: Five controlled studies show arrays are reached at the distance-matched random rate, and large displacement or large gaps refill LESS often soon. The engine rewards displacement, gap size and HTF origin in the array density (line 687), biasing selection toward the arrays least likely to be revisited within H. A liquidity-first prior matches ICT and the S/R evidence.
proposals.spec: Keep quality only as a creation gate (fvgQMin/obQMin). evaluate() array branch (687-688): dens = 0.40 + 0.30*coil + 0.30*induce (no qual, no HTF +0.20); mult *= (1 - 0.5*fill) * arrPrior * (sz > bigDisp ? bigPen : 1). New Level field sz = zone height/ATR at birth for FVG/HTF-FVG/gaps (set at 1874/1884/1862), or leg/ATR for OB/BRK (1703/1744). New inputs: arrPrior 0.90, bigDisp 1.0 ATR, bigPen 0.85. Size-tercile calibration (bins 0.35/0.8 ATR) via a generic f_ctxMult helper (shrinkage n/(n+30), bounds 0.8-1.2) using Trial.szBin stored at f_openTrial (1426) and booked in f_book (1461). Full panel (2410-2418): show 'exp xx%' = stPE/n next to each family's hit %, the same test the external studies use. Non-repainting: confirmed-bar block only.
proposals.risk: Instruments where arrays genuinely outperform are under-weighted until calibration catches up (about 20-30 trials per family; bounded). Arrays are still selected when they are clearly the best candidate (Clean 'Target: BEFVG' look unchanged).

proposals.title: Correct breaker definition (sweep by the leg leaving the block), add wick-raid breakers, optional mitigation blocks
proposals.rationale: ICT verbatim: 'Bearish Breaker Block is a bearish range or Down Close Candle in the most recent Swing Low prior to an Old High being violated.' The engine requires the OB's own origin to have swept a 20-bar extreme (tookL/tookH), which is the wrong side. This drops canonical breakers, keeps a non-ICT subset, and misses wick-raid breakers. Wrong labels are a visible correctness issue for an ICT user.
proposals.spec: (1) Lines 1706/1747: push every BOS-created OB to obTrk (the BOS leg already violated an old extreme); tookL/tookH become a +0.15 quality bonus. (2) Step 1 (~1542): raidUp = not na(obSwingH) and high > obSwingH and close <= obSwingH and not raidH. On a raid, find the bullish OB candidate at the leg low as step 8 does (lowest low since obSwingHBar, then the down-close candle in loI..loI+5) and push Zone(dir=+1, qual=0.5, tookLiq=true) without a pool level. Step 7 (1651) then flips it to a bearish breaker on close < bottom. Reset raidH when step 9 sets a new obSwingH. Mirror for lows. (3) Optional input 'Mitigation Blocks' (default off): store OB candidates at confirmed pivot lows with the prior pivot high; if the next pivot high is lower and a later close breaks the candidate bottom, create kind 7 with qual*0.7 and Level.variant=1 (label BEMB/BUMB). (4) Split grp 3 stats into OB vs BRK (or f_ctxMult on variant).
proposals.risk: More array candidates. Contained by ICTPD-1's prior, poolMax (1951) and the obTrk cap of 30 (1749). Mitigation-block conventions disagree across sources.

proposals.title: Fill-ladder probabilities (CE / full fill) for array targets plus ledger depth stats
proposals.rationale: Traders plan partials at the near edge, CE and full fill. The empirical ladder is large on HTFs (BTC 4H within 24 h: touch 71.8% -> CE 62.3% -> full 54.2%). The engine already has the empirical surface (f_potModel) to price each level at O(1) cost.
proposals.spec: LIVE READOUTS (2066-2067), array target: dCE = max(0, side==1 ? price-close : close-price) (price = original mid); dFull = max(0, side==1 ? oTop-close : close-oBot); potCE = f_potModel(dCE, side, potMu*side); potFull likewise. Show 'CE xx% · FULL yy%' in the Clean label tooltip (2206) and on a Terminal HUD line. Ledger: keep array trials that hit the near edge in a small list until bar0+H, with Trial fields ce/far and flags ceHit/fullHit; report 'tap->CE x% -> FULL y%' in the Full view (arrays ladN/ladCE/ladFull).
proposals.risk: Minimal. Tooltip and HUD text only; the Clean look is unchanged.

proposals.title: IRL <-> ERL delivery phase with arrays as waypoints
proposals.rationale: ICT's central rule for which liquidity comes next: after an external raid that rejects, the draw is internal (gaps); after an internal rebalance that holds, the draw is the opposite external pool. The engine models direction after raids, not the target type. Evidence is weak but the effect is directly measurable by the ledger.
proposals.spec: State: var irlSide/irlBar/erlSide/erlBar and a pending array (side, near, far, bar). ERL event in step 3 (1580): if a hit liquidity level has src>=1 or eqCount>0 or stack>0, evt == -side sets irlSide := -side, and evt == side sets erlSide := side. IRL event: an array hit stores pending; within 6 bars, a close >= 0.5 ATR away from near in direction -side without closing beyond far sets erlSide := -side; a close beyond far clears pending. Expiry after phaseLen (default 2*H). Step 17 before evaluate: arrays on irlSide x phB (1.15), liquidity on irlSide x0.92; liquidity on erlSide x phB, arrays on erlSide x0.90. Once 20 or more trials exist per phase, phB is replaced by f_ctxMult. Trial.ph in {0,1,2}; Full view row 'PHASE IRL k/n vs exp · ERL k/n vs exp'. Tooltip for an array target names the best pool beyond it ('then -> BSL @ x, PoT y%').
proposals.risk: Can amplify wrong reads after genuine breakouts. Mitigated by requiring a rejection for IRL, bounded multipliers and phase expiry.

proposals.title: IPDA 20/40/60-day extremes as external-range liquidity (no request call)
proposals.rationale: These are ICT's canonical HTF external range and the levels where Donchian/Turtle breakout stops cluster (Osler 2003 mechanism). PDH/PWH and pivots do not cover them. Exact anchors come free from the existing day tracker.
proposals.spec: After line 961: var arrays dH/dHB/dL/dLB of the last 60 completed days, filled on pdNew from f_rangeTrack outputs (945), only when timeframe.in_seconds() <= 86400. f_nDay(n, isHigh) returns [px, bar] over the last n entries. Step 10 (after 1799), on pdNew: for n in array.from(20,40,60) with size >= n, f_pushExt(extReg, hx, true, src 8/9/10, hb, (hx-lx)/atr*0.5, sqrt(n*86400/chartS)) and likewise for lows. f_tierW: 8=>0.84, 9=>0.88, 10=>0.95. f_levelName: '20D H/L', '40D H/L', '60D H/L'. Duplicates merge and the higher tier wins (1211-1225).
proposals.risk: Registry crowding (cap 60, 1813). Low-TF charts with under 20 days of history get nothing (graceful).

proposals.title: Opening gaps (NWOG / NDOG / RTH overnight gap) as imbalance targets
proposals.rationale: Widely watched ICT references with documented, strongly size-dependent fill base rates (SPY same-day: 78-80% for 0.1-0.25% gaps vs 26-33% for gaps over 1%). They are not detected today and cost no request call.
proposals.spec: sesBrk = timeframe.isintraday and time - time[1] > 1.5*timeframe.in_seconds()*1000; gHi = max(open, close[1]); gLo = min(open, close[1]); require gHi-gLo >= max(gapMin*ATR, 2*mintick). On the confirmed break bar the zone is the far half (near edge = CE): a gap up creates kind 9 (side -1), zone [gLo, CE], price = CE, if close > CE; a gap down creates kind 8 (side +1), zone [CE, gHi], if close < CE. src = 7 if timeframe.change('W') (NWOG) else 6 (NDOG). Keep the last 5 weekly and 3 daily via id arrays. f_newLevel side map (1085): add kind 8 -> +1. grp() (636): kinds 8/9 -> family 2. Names NWOG/NDOG. Non-active delivery on a CE touch. Apply ICTPD-1's large-size penalty (gap-and-go).
proposals.risk: Feed quirks (FX rollover bars) create small spurious breaks; the size gate filters them. No gaps on crypto (graceful).

proposals.title: Adaptive premium/discount side prior learned by the ledger
proposals.rationale: ICT says 'longs only in discount, targets in premium', but strong literature (George & Hwang 2004) shows continuation near highs at long horizons, and there are no intraday statistics. Learn the effect per chart rather than hard-code it.
proposals.spec: Zone = quartile of close within the IPDA 20-day range (ICTPD-5), falling back to htfRH/htfRL (923). 8 cells = side x zone. Trial.pz stored at open and booked into pzN/pzK/pzE. Step 17: lv.mult *= f_ctxMult(cell(lv.side, zoneNow), 0.85, 1.15, nMin 40). Optional static input 'Premium/Discount Prior' (default 0 = off). Terminal row 'IPDA20 PREM 72%'; Full view 'BUY-side from DISC k/n vs exp; from PREM k/n vs exp'.
proposals.risk: Slow learning with 8 cells; bounded impact.

proposals.title: iFVG retest honesty stats against a two-barrier race baseline
proposals.rationale: The reference product sells 'iFVG continuation', but a controlled S&P daily test found iFVG retests hold exactly as often as random zones (38% vs 38%, 47% vs 47%). Users should see the real hold rate on their own chart.
proposals.spec: On the first retest of an active iFVG (step 6, 1630-1644; bearish case: high >= z.bottom) open a light record: tgt = touch - 1.0*ATR, fail = close > z.top, expiry H. Baseline p0 = f_race(1.0*atr, z.top - touch, potSig, -potMu) (line 447): the hold probability of a random level with the same geometry. Accumulate n, k and the sum of p0; Full view shows 'iFVG HOLD k/n (exp p0)'. Needs Zone.retested and a parallel array or a small type.
proposals.risk: Approximation: the race uses touches while invalidation uses closes. Document it.

proposals.title: Rejection-block metadata on liquidity targets: near-miss statistic and wick-zone band
proposals.rationale: ICT/RB practice trims targets to the body extreme of old highs/lows. The engine deliberately counts a sweep only when price trades through, which stays. Measuring how often price reaches the wick zone but fails to sweep informs take-profit placement.
proposals.spec: Level.body at chart-pivot creation: BSL math.max(open[pivLen], close[pivLen]) (1762), SSL math.min(...) (1774); na for external pools. Trial.rb and flag rbHit set in f_step (1434) when high >= rb (BSL) or low <= rb (SSL). At booking, among expired misses report 'near-miss in wick zone x%'. Optional thin RB band in the Terminal style.
proposals.risk: None to selection.

proposals.title: Liquidity-void merge of consecutive same-direction FVGs
proposals.rationale: Displacement legs print 2-4 adjacent FVGs. The engine creates a level for each, which duplicates candidates, risks flicker between adjacent zones, and gives a CE for one sub-gap only. ICT treats the leg as one void; open-source SMC libraries join consecutive gaps.
proposals.spec: Step 13 (1868-1886): var lastBuId/lastBuBar (and the bearish pair). If a new bullish FVG forms at bar_index == lastBuBar+1 and that level is still in the pool with fill == 0, extend it: top := max(top, low), oTop := top, price := (oTop+oBot)/2, qual := max(qual, qU), sz recomputed. Otherwise create a new level as now. fvgTrk (iFVG tracking) stays per-gap.
proposals.risk: A merged void's CE is deeper, so non-active CE delivery takes longer (intended).

result.summary: The ICT time and price concepts change the probability and timing of a level being taken through one dominant channel: the intraday and weekly volatility clock. This is strong evidence (Andersen-Bollerslev). On 16 years of hourly data the busiest hour is 2.1-4.0x wider than the quietest, and the FOMC hour runs 5.2x a normal hour, NFP 2.7x and CPI 2.1x. I simulated a random walk whose variance follows those published hourly profiles, and it reproduces most ICT time 'facts' within a few points. Examples: Asian-range breaks, 'NY takes London H/L', the hour of the daily high, range completion, and ES HOD/LOD timing. 'Red first hour → red day' (66.2% observed vs 65-66% under the random walk) is pure overlap arithmetic, and the weekly 'Tuesday low' folklore must beat the arcsine baseline (Mon 29.5 / Tue 14.1 / Wed 12.8 / Thu 14.1 / Fri 29.5%). Reversal-timing claims (Judas swing, AMD manipulation leg) fail mechanical tests. The FX Asian-range first-break fade is 49.4% (n = 9,598, not significant), the London opening-range follow-through is 50.3% (n = 92,947), crypto continues 55-58%, and equity intraday momentum is real but small (R² 1.6%). The midnight open is the only time anchor with a measured excess: 65.6-68.0% RTH revisit across 9,226 days vs 52-61% under the random walk. Macros, Silver Bullet (the one mechanical test: 38.9% win rate at 1:1, a net loss), quarterly theory, IPDA ranges and CBDR/Asian SD rungs have no supporting evidence. The engine's biggest time defect is the time-blind trailing σ (potSig, line 916) and the hour-pooled empirical surface behind PoT, reach and race. On a 5m chart a displayed 20% PoT is really about 50-55% at 08:30-09:30 ET and about 9-14% in the afternoon. The same blindness biases the ledger's random baseline, so EDGE can be inflated by killzone timing. Two correctness bugs: session membership uses time(), which tests only the bar's open (doc-verified), so on the default 1H chart the NY AM range misses 09:30-10:00 and the NY open anchor is the 10:00 open; and 10:00-11:00 ET, the peak-volatility hour for US indices, is classed OFF-KZ. The fixed killzone affinity multipliers (f_kzAff) double-count what the volatility clock explains and are contradicted in FX, where the Asian range is respected more than a random walk would predict. Best proposals: a learned volatility clock for PoT, reach, race and the surface; a time-aware ledger with a Brier A/B so the gain is measurable on the chart; session-window correctness plus ONH/ONL and NY PM sources; and session-horizon PoT with an ETA in clock time.

concepts.name: Intraday/weekly volatility clock (intraday periodicity)
concepts.definition: r_t = σ_day · s(τ_t) · z_t, where s(τ) is a deterministic periodic variance factor by NY time-of-day bucket (and weekday) and σ_day is a slowly varying level (Andersen-Bollerslev). The forward first-passage probability depends on the variance remaining in the window, V = Σ σ²_day · s²(τ_k), not on the bar count.
concepts.dolRole: Sets how far price can travel in the next H bars or before the session end, which drives PoT, reachability, race odds and ETA. It is the quantitative form of 'killzones'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Andersen & Bollerslev 1997/1998; fxbacktest 922,937 H1 bars: peak/quiet 2.1-4.0x (EURUSD 27.7 vs 8.1 pips, US30 4.0x, US100 3.9x); release hours FOMC 5.21x, NFP 2.69x, CPI 2.08x (3,963 releases). My PoT-error computation: on 5m with H = 30 the trailing σ is 1.9-2.1x too low at 08:30-09:30 ET and 0.76-0.88x after 11:45.
concepts.engineNotes: potSig = ta.stdev(ta.change(close), potLen) (916) feeds f_pot in f_potModel (1304), f_potBase (1315), the race (1360-1363) and proximity reach (665, 1948). The empirical surface (1061, 1527-1532) is normalised by atr[H] and pooled across all hours.

concepts.name: Killzones
concepts.definition: NY-time windows (DST-aware): Asia 20:00-00:00; London 02:00-05:00; NY AM 07:00-10:00 (index variant 08:30-11:00); London close 10:00-12:00; NY lunch 12:00-13:00/13:30; NY PM 13:30-16:00. A bar is in a killzone if [bar open, bar close) overlaps the window.
concepts.dolRole: Says WHEN raids are likely, i.e. when the remaining variance is high. Not an independent selector of WHICH level.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Strong as times of elevated activity (E1, E2). As extra raid probability beyond volatility: none (my random-walk baselines).
concepts.engineNotes: 223-226 and 970-976 define Asia, London, NY AM 07-10 and NY PM. No London-close or index NY AM window, so 10:00-11:00 ET (the peak hour for US indices) is OFF-KZ, which doubles hysteresis (hystEff 976). The in/out switch is binary.

concepts.name: Killzone affinity ('London raids Asia, NY raids London/PD')
concepts.definition: ICT session sequence: Asia builds a range, London takes one side, NY takes London's or the previous day's extremes.
concepts.dolRole: Claims a session-specific preference for which pool is taken next.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A random walk on the volatility clock reproduces it. Asian range broken later the same day, high/low/both/neither: EURUSD observed 68.2/68.4/37.7/1.0 vs random walk 74.1/74.7/48.9/0.1; US100 observed 82.0/73.8/56.2/0.4 vs 75.7/76.1/51.9/0.1. NY breaks London (YM): single break 83.2% observed vs 77-78%. FX double breaks run BELOW random, i.e. the Asian range is respected more.
concepts.engineNotes: f_kzAff (597-602), applied at 1941: fixed ×1.05-1.20 for session and PD pools regardless of distance or remaining variance. Unsupported, double-counts the volatility clock, and makes DOL choices (and ledger trials) cluster in killzones.

concepts.name: Session ranges as liquidity (Asia/London/NY AM/lunch/PM/overnight)
concepts.definition: The high and low printed inside a fixed NY-time window, pushed as a pool once the window closes. Overnight/Globex 18:00-09:30 gives ONH/ONL.
concepts.dolRole: Very frequent next targets. Probability is governed by distance and remaining variance.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Asian range: at least one side broken ~99% of days (FX) and 99.6% (indices), 4,162 days. NQ ONH/ONL (2,827 days): at least one broken 94.2%; only high 38.7, only low 32.6, both 22.9, none 5.8%; open above the ON midpoint → high breaks first 76.2%; 68.7% of first breaks by 10:00.
concepts.engineNotes: Asia (2000-0000), London (0200-0500) and NY AM (0930-1200) are tracked (107-109, 835-863, 948-950) and pushed at 1800-1809. Bug: time() tests only the bar open (sessions.md line 47), so on a 1H chart NY AM starts at the 10:00 bar and misses 09:30-10:00. Missing: ONH/ONL, NY PM and lunch ranges.

concepts.name: Midnight open / true day open
concepts.definition: The open of the 00:00 NY bar, extended through the day. The 'true day' starts at midnight NY; on bullish days the low should form below the midnight open early, then price distributes above it.
concepts.dolRole: An early-session magnet and target, and a premium/discount split of the day.
concepts.evidenceNotes: tradingstats, 9,226 days NQ/ES/YM: RTH revisit 68.0/65.7/65.6%; near 85-87% vs far 42-46%; median retrace time 09:41-09:48. My random-walk baseline is 52-61%, so the excess is about 5-15 pp. Plausibly the reversal of overnight drift (NY Fed SR917: the 09:00-10:00 ET return is -1.2 bp, t = 2.6).
concepts.engineNotes: Used only as a confluence anchor: sessMid 220, f_sessOpen 798-803, midOpen 964, anchors 1931. Never a target. Stays na on charts above 1H, because no bar opens inside 0000-0100.

concepts.name: 08:30 / 09:30 / weekly / session true opens
concepts.definition: Opening prices at the 08:30 release time, the 09:30 cash open, Sunday 18:00 or Monday 18:00 (the true week open), and the quarterly-theory session true opens 19:30/01:30/07:30/13:30.
concepts.dolRole: Bias split lines. 08:30 marks a known volatility spike.
concepts.evidenceNotes: 08:30 is strong as a volatility time (E3) and untested as a level. The other opens have no studies.
concepts.engineNotes: London 02:00 and NY 09:30 opens are confluence anchors (221-222, 965-966). On 1H charts the 0930-1030 window captures the 10:00 open (misaligned). No 08:30 or weekly open.

concepts.name: Algorithmic macros
concepts.definition: About 20-minute windows in NY time: 02:33-03:00, 04:03-04:30, 08:50-09:10, 09:50-10:10, 10:50-11:10, 11:50-12:10, 13:10-13:40, 15:15-15:45. Price is expected to sweep nearby liquidity and/or rebalance an FVG.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed fine timing of raids.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No published test. LuxAlgo notes the windows coincide with 10:00 ET data releases and round-time flows. A 15-30 min volatility clock captures any real burst.
concepts.engineNotes: Absent, correctly. Should not be a scoring term; at most a ledger tag.

concepts.name: Silver Bullet
concepts.definition: Windows 03:00-04:00, 10:00-11:00 and 14:00-15:00 NY. After a liquidity sweep, enter on the first FVG formed by displacement toward the draw and target the next pool.
concepts.dolRole: A claimed high-probability time window for a draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Negative: a mechanical test of the 10:00 window gave 108 trades, a 38.9% win rate at 1:1, and a net loss (tradestar).
concepts.engineNotes: Absent; not recommended as scoring.

concepts.name: Power of 3 (AMD) and Judas swing
concepts.definition: Each candle runs accumulation, then a manipulation leg against the eventual direction (an early extreme beyond the midnight or session open), then distribution. A Judas swing is that leg early in a session; it must fail with displacement back through structure.
concepts.dolRole: Claims the first raid of a session is a reversal signal pointing at the opposite liquidity.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Asian-range first-break fade in FX 49.4% (n = 9,598, z -1.25, ns); crypto continues 55-58%; London opening-range follow-through 50.3% (n = 92,947); post-release first-15-minute direction holds 63.5% after 4h; G10 FX sweeps favour continuation (ict_liq E7).
concepts.engineNotes: liqEvt (1580-1582) hard-codes 'close back inside = reversal' at any time of day. ict_liq ICT-2 proposes learning its sign; session-conditioning is a possible extension.

concepts.name: CBDR / Asian range / Flout standard-deviation projections
concepts.definition: CBDR 14:00-20:00 NY (ideally under 40 pips); 1 'SD' = the range height; rungs U_k = H + kR and D_k = L - kR, k ∈ {1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4}; the London extreme is expected at 1-3 SD, 4 SD on news. The Asian range (20:00-00:00) is projected 2-4 SD. Flout = CBDR plus Asia (about 15:00-00:00).
concepts.dolRole: Claims where the day's high or low will form.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No test found. The underlying size fact is a volatility ratio: the Asian session holds 47.9% of EURUSD's daily range and 36.5% of US100's (fxbacktest), which the clock already provides.
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended as targets. At most optional confluence anchors tested by the ledger.

concepts.name: Quarterly theory
concepts.definition: The day in 6h quarters (18-00, 00-06, 06-12, 12-18 NY), each split into 90-minute quarters, applied recursively to week, month and year. Phases AMDX or XAMD. The true open is the Q2 open (midnight for the day).
concepts.dolRole: Claimed phase timing of manipulation vs delivery.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No validation (LuxAlgo); AMDX vs XAMD is discretionary.
concepts.engineNotes: Not implemented; not recommended.

concepts.name: Daily and weekly profiles / weekday of the weekly extreme
concepts.definition: Templates: London/NY reversal or continuation days; Classic Tuesday low/high of the week, Wednesday low/high, Consolidation Thursday reversal, Seek & Destroy Friday, etc.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed day-of-week priors for when the weekly extreme and reversals occur.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Arcsine null: Mon 29.5 / Tue 14.1 / Wed 12.8 / Thu 14.1 / Fri 29.5%; weekly low in by Tuesday's close 43.6%. Aldous: 746 S&P 20-day blocks match a random walk. The real effect is volatility: Monday NY range 60.81 vs Friday 76.98 (ES); EURUSD Monday 68.1 vs Thursday 84.7 pips.
concepts.engineNotes: No weekday logic. The Monday-volatility factor belongs in the clock (TIME-1). The named profiles are not recommended.

concepts.name: IPDA 20/40/60-day data ranges and quarterly shifts
concepts.definition: The highest high and lowest low of the last 20/40/60 trading days (daily candles) and their equilibria. Untaken extremes are 20-60 day draws ('cast forward' from the month of the last liquidity grab or MSS). A quarterly shift is a directional change around a quarter turn.
concepts.dolRole: Higher-timeframe objective levels for swing horizons.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No touch study. N-day extremes are widely watched (weak by analogy).
concepts.engineNotes: PWH/PWL (1795-1799), HTF pivots (1782-1789) and htfEQ (968) exist; no N-day extremes or 60-day equilibrium.

concepts.name: Seasonal tendencies / calendar drifts
concepts.definition: Asset seasonals, turn-of-month, the pre-FOMC drift, the overnight drift (ES 02:00-03:00 ET).
concepts.dolRole: A drift tilt toward one side.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Overnight drift (NY Fed SR917): 1.5 bp/h at 02:00-03:00 ET, t = 7.1, 3.7% a year; opening hour -1.2 bp. Effect sizes are 0.1-0.2σ per hour or less, negligible for PoT.
concepts.engineNotes: potMu (917) carries a generic trailing drift. Not worth modelling.

concepts.name: Scheduled news times (08:30/10:00/14:00 releases)
concepts.definition: Known release times create variance spikes: FOMC hour about 5x, NFP about 2.7x, CPI about 2.1-2.7x normal.
concepts.dolRole: Large, foreseeable jumps in reachability.
concepts.evidenceNotes: fxbacktest, 3,963 releases 2007-2026; NFP surprise size does not predict range; Andersen-Bollerslev-Diebold-Vega 2003.
concepts.engineNotes: Pine has no calendar. The clock learns the average 08:30/10:00 bump; FOMC-type events need a manual input (TIME-7).

concepts.name: Intraday momentum / session opening drive
concepts.definition: The first half-hour return (from the previous close to 10:00) predicts the last half-hour return (SPY, 1993-2013).
concepts.dolRole: A late-session directional tilt for equity indices; the measured opposite of the Judas reversal.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou JFE 2018: slope 0.069, R² 1.6% (2.6% with the 12th half-hour), OOS R² 1.2-1.7%. Absent in FX and commodity futures. Small effect.
concepts.engineNotes: Only a generic displacement term in D (1536-1541, 1893), half-life 12 bars.

concepts.name: Arcsine law for timing of highs and lows
concepts.definition: For Brownian motion on [0, T] the time of the maximum has density 1/(π√(t(T-t))), in business (variance) time. Window edges are over-represented.
concepts.dolRole: The null model any 'the high forms at X' claim must beat.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ES HOD at 09:30-09:45 observed 17.2% (mypivots, 1,586 days) vs 12.3% calendar-time arcsine and 17.7% with a 2x open variance. EURUSD hour of the high observed 8.8%/7.9% vs random walk 10.7%/7.0%.
concepts.engineNotes: Not an engine feature. It shows that hard-coded time priors are mostly artefacts.

concepts.name: Time-aware ledger baseline and PoT calibration
concepts.definition: Grade hits against a random-level baseline matched on distance AND forward variance (time of day), and score the displayed PoT with a Brier score and calibration.
concepts.dolRole: Measures whether target choice beats chance net of timing, and whether PoT is honest.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Standard methodology; the bias mechanism follows from E18 plus killzone clustering of trial starts.
concepts.engineNotes: f_potBase (1314-1322) is time-blind. Trials (2037-2045) cluster in killzones because of f_kzAff and off-KZ hysteresis, so EDGE can be inflated by timing. Trials do not store the model PoT, so PoT calibration is never measured.

concepts.name: Session-horizon PoT and ETA in clock time
concepts.definition: P(touch before killzone end / 16:00 / 17:00) using the remaining clock variance; ETA = the time when V(τ) reaches (d/0.6745)², the median first passage.
concepts.dolRole: Answers 'will this be taken this session, and roughly when'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Same model as the clock. Observed timing is clock-like: midnight-open retrace median 09:41-09:48; 68.7% of ON breaks by 10:00.
concepts.engineNotes: ETA|hit is the median bars-to-hit of past hits at a similar distance (2106-2126), in bars; the horizon H is a fixed bar count.

proposals.title: Learned volatility clock (time-of-day × weekday) for PoT, reach, race and the empirical surface
proposals.rationale: PoT, reach, race and reach bands assume the next H bars behave like the last 50 (potSig, line 916). On a 5m chart with the defaults a displayed 20% PoT is really about 50-55% at 08:30-09:30 ET and about 9-14% in the afternoon. A learned clock is the quantitative, symbol-specific form of killzones, macros and session timing. It replaces ad-hoc time priors with one coherent mechanism.
proposals.spec:
Inputs (G_POT): useClk (bool, true), clkMin (15/30/60, default 30), clkMem (days, 40), useDow (bool). Derived: bkMin = max(clkMin, chart minutes); clkOK = intraday and bkMin <= 240 and 1440 % bkMin == 0; NBK = 1440/bkMin; bpb = bars per bucket.
State: clkA[NBK] time-of-day factor (init 1), clkD[7] weekday factor, clkC[7*NBK] bar counts (open-cell mask), clkL deseasonalised per-bar variance, clkDy days seen.
Learning (global, barstate.isconfirmed only): bucket cB = floor((hour(time,tz)*60 + minute(time,tz))/bkMin); cD = dayofweek(time,tz)-1; r2 = log(close/close[1])^2; s0 = a[cB]*c[cD]; x = min(25, r2/(clkL*s0)); a[cB] *= 1 + aB*(x-1) with aB = 1 - 0.5^(1/(clkMem*bpb)); same for c[cD] with 5x slower memory; clkL EWMA of min(r2/s0, 25*clkL) with alpha 2/(potLen+1). On timeframe.change('D'): renormalise a and c to a bar-weighted mean of 1 and fold the scale into clkL; shrink thin buckets toward 1.
Forward variance f_fwdVar(h): walk forward from the current bucket over open cells (count >= 0.3 * days/7 * bpb), summing bars * a*c, times clkL. Cost about H/bpb iterations, or O(log) with daily prefix sums.
Wiring: sigH = clkDy >= 5 ? close*sqrt(fwdV/H) : potSig; replaces potSig at 1304, 1315, 1360 and 1948 (evaluate sig). Phase B: store fwdSd = close*sqrt(fwdV); step 0 (1528-1532) normalises excursions by fwdSd[H] instead of atr[H] (z-grid 5/NB); f_empPoT queries z = d/fwdSd; reach bands convert z*fwdSd/atr. A z-surface is horizon-invariant under Brownian motion, so it also serves TIME-4. All updates run on confirmed bars, so it stays non-repainting; no new request calls. Verified built-ins: hour/minute/dayofweek(time, timezone).
proposals.risk: Thin buckets on short histories: mitigated by shrinkage, a 5-day gate, and learning from all loaded bars rather than only calcBars. Holidays and early closes overstate V. The US/UK DST mismatch smears the London bucket (an optional clock-timezone input helps). Phase B changes the surface units, so verify the reach-band display. Loop guard needed over weekends.

proposals.title: Time-aware ledger: clock-based random baseline, PoT calibration (Brier) A/B, killzone-split EDGE
proposals.rationale: pBase (1314-1322) is time-blind, and DOL choices cluster in killzones (f_kzAff 1941, off-KZ hysteresis 976), so EDGE partly measures timing rather than level selection. The displayed PoT, the number traders act on, is never checked. This makes TIME-1's value directly measurable on the user's own chart.
proposals.spec:
Trial type (375-395) gets: pMod (displayed PoT at open, with the clock), pAlt (the same without the clock), kz0 (killzone at open). f_openTrial (1426): pBase via the clock-aware f_potBase.
f_book (1461): new calSt array [n, Σy, Σp, Σ(y-pMod)^2, Σ(y-pAlt)^2, block-Σd, closed-block Σd^2, blockId], with d = (y-pMod)^2 - (y-pAlt)^2, reusing the 2H-block cluster variance of cluSt (1463-1469) for a robust z of the Brier difference. kzN/kzK/kzE arrays (size 6, indexed by kz0+1) give hit-vs-baseline per killzone.
Panel (Terminal, Accuracy = Full): 'PoT CAL pred 44% · obs 46% · n 212', 'BRIER .212 vs .231 no-clock · z 2.4', 'EDGE by KZ LDN +5.8 · NYAM +6.3 · OFF +1.9 pp'. Confirmed bars only; O(1) per booking.
proposals.risk: Overlapping trials share price paths (handled by the block variance). Small n early. The extra pAlt computation happens only at trial open.

proposals.title: Session-window correctness and coverage: overlap test, London-close / index NY AM killzone, ONH/ONL and NY PM sources
proposals.rationale: time(timeframe.period, sess, tz) tests only the bar open (docs: concepts/sessions.md line 47). On the default 1H execution chart the NY AM range starts at the 10:00 bar (missing 09:30-10:00), the NY open anchor is the 10:00 open, and NY PM starts at 14:00. 10:00-11:00 ET, the peak-volatility hour for US index futures, is OFF-KZ. The most-watched index-futures pools (ONH/ONL, broken 94.2% of RTH days) are missing.
proposals.spec:
(a) Replace not na(time(timeframe.period, sess, tz)) at 799, 836 and 971-974 with a minute-of-day overlap test. Parse each input.session string once with str.substring/str.tonumber (sM, eM). f_inWin tests the half-open interval [b0, b0 + chart minutes) against [sM, eM), handling midnight-wrapping windows and bars that run past midnight (two-arc test). An 'exact' flag (bar opens at sM) marks approximate anchors (≈ in the HUD and tooltip). Optional exact 09:30 open on 1H/4H via request.security_lower_tf(syminfo.tickerid, '30', [time, open]) read on confirmed bars.
(b) Add kzLC input.session('1000-1200', 'London Close Killzone') as kz 5; change the NY AM default to 0700-1100 or offer an index preset 0830-1100; extend f_kzName.
(c) New registry sources via f_sessTrack with the overlap test: sessON '1800-0930' → src 8 'ONH/ONL' (tier 0.62); sessPM '1330-1600' → src 9 'PM H/L' (0.55); optional lunch '1200-1330' → src 10 (0.45). Update f_tierW (505-516), f_levelName/f_shortName (518-541) and the src comment (316); push at session end like 1800-1809; consider raising the registry cap at 1813 by 10.
proposals.risk: Including a straddling bar adds pre-session prices to the NY range on 1H (flagged by exact). More registry entries. f_pushExt de-duplicates identical prices.

proposals.title: PoT by session end and an ETA in clock time
proposals.rationale: Traders ask 'will the PDH go in NY AM / before the close?', not 'within 30 bars'. Timing is predictable from the clock: midnight-open retraces have a median of 09:41-09:48, and 68.7% of ON breaks happen by 10:00. A PoT that decays toward the close is the natural stale-target filter (the ICT 'time stop').
proposals.spec:
Inputs (G_POT): potHor ('Bars (H)', 'Killzone End', 'NY Close 16:00', 'Day End 17:00'); showEta (bool).
Bars to the horizon hS: the f_fwdVar grid walk counting open-cell bars to the end minute; V = f_fwdVar(hS). PoT_S = f_pot(d, close*sqrt(V/hS), mu, hS), or the z-surface P(Z >= d/(close*sqrt V)) from TIME-1 phase B.
ETA: walk until V(τ) >= (d/0.6745)^2 (driftless median first passage), also an 80% time at (d/1.2816)^2. On barstate.islast, convert bars to clock time with time(timeframe.period, '', tz, -k) (k <= 500) and str.format_time(t, 'HH:mm', tz).
