proposals.risk: Fewer displacement events; if REG-3 gates D overall this is a small refinement. The per-series results are mixed, so keep the change behind the input and let the ledger decide.

proposals.title: Measured-move shadow baselines and breakout-context features (zero prior) in the candidate ledger
proposals.rationale: Traders trained on Brooks, Bulkowski or ICT ask whether the engine beats simply aiming at the measured move. The random-level baseline answers 'better than chance', not 'better than my rule'. The small T3/T4 effects (0 to +3 pp: big breakout bars, range-breakout state, close-back-inside) and the Fibonacci-confluence claim belong in a learner with zero prior weight, not in hand-set multipliers.
proposals.spec: 1) With COMP-3's shadow-selector infrastructure, open hidden trials alongside each DOL trial for (a) MM 1.0 of the current zigzag leg (PA-1 ladder), (b) the nearest draw-side pool, (c) ICT -1 SD; grade them like DOL trials (hit within H vs pBase). Panel: 'vs MM-rule +x pp · vs nearest +y pp'. 2) Add to the CAL-3 / CAL-4 feature vector (prior 0): last breakout bar body/ATR and close location; 20-bar range-break flag and range width in ATR; bars since the last range breakout and whether it closed back inside within 5 bars; zigzag leg progress u/delta and y/delta; a 'within 0.1 ATR of MM 1.0 / EXT -0.27 / -0.62 / -1' flag. Capped as in CAL-3 (256 probes).
proposals.risk: More per-candidate state; it depends on COMP-3 and CAL-3/4 being built first.

result.summary:
The classic reference levels in this domain are not magnets beyond their distance. I ran 8 tests against the engine ledger's own baseline: a random level at the same ATR distance from price. Data were about 1,500 CME futures days and 3,300 BTC days on 1h bars, plus SPX/NDX/BTC daily bars. Firecrawl had no credits left, so the published evidence comes from WebSearch summaries plus the sibling study reports.
- Daily floor, Camarilla, Fibonacci, Woodie and DeMark pivots are reached at the random rate (-3 to +1.2 pp), the same as range-scaled placebo levels. Monthly, quarterly and yearly opens and monthly pivots are reached less often than random (QOPEN -1.9 pp, z -3.8 at 5 days; MOPEN -3.2 pp, z -3.0 at 20 days). Prior month/quarter/year highs and lows, 52-week extremes and 20/60-day extremes are at baseline.
- The main actionable finding: weekly floor pivots (PP/R1/S1) and the weekly open act as path barriers. Each one between price and a pool cuts its 24h sweep rate by about 5-6 pp (CME z -5.3, BTC z -6.9), roughly -0.25 logit per level. The effect grows with the number crossed (BTC: 1 level -4 pp, 2 levels -11 pp), holds at H=8 and H=24, and survives distance, range-position, age and source controls. Daily pivots and placebo levels show no such effect. This fits the strong literature: published support/resistance interrupts intraday trends (Osler 2000) and sits where order-book depth peaks (Kavajecz & Odders-White 2004).
- The engine's Confluence pillar (weight 15) has the wrong sign. No anchor family is consistently positive. PD/PW pools used as anchors give -4.8 pp on CME (z -3.6), and session opens / day EQ are neutral to -3.3 pp. Weekly levels (-4 to -7 pp) and round numbers (-1 to -1.4 pp), which siblings propose to add, are negative. The sibling calib_ml study found the same (-0.25 logit).
- Small real effects: prior-day value levels near price (settlement, CPR, PP, prior-day VWAP) are reached 1.5-4 pp more often than random. Large opening gaps (at least 0.5 daily ATR) fill more often than random (+7.9 pp, z 4.5, NDX). Small gaps fill no more than their distance predicts.
- The moving session VWAP is hit mostly for mechanical reasons, so it must not become a static target.
- Folklore fails: a narrow CPR does not predict a trend day (the effect is reversed or inconsistent), and 'above pivot/VWAP/open = bullish' adds nothing beyond where price sits in the prior range.
- Best changes: a weekly-reference barrier in score and PoT (CL-1), a neutral confluence pillar (CL-2), per-symbol context lifts in the shadow ledger (CL-3), and optionally a gap-gated prior-settlement target (CL-4).

concepts.name: Classic floor pivots (daily PP/R1/S1/R2/S2/R3/S3)
concepts.definition: PP=(H+L+C)/3 of the prior session; R1=2PP-L, S1=2PP-H, R2=PP+R, S2=PP-R, R3=H+2(PP-L), S3=L-2(H-PP), with R=H-L. The levels stay fixed for the next session. C is the settlement or last trade, and RTH and ETH session templates give different levels.
concepts.dolRole: Practitioners use R1/S1 as first targets or fades and R2/S2 as extensions; 'above PP = bullish'. As targets they would say which level price draws to next.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T1, distance-matched (CME 1h ~1,500 days; BTC ~3,300 days): R1 -0.1/-1.5 pp, S1 -0.5/-1.1, R2 -3.0 (z -3.1 CME), S2 -0.7/+1.0. Range-scaled placebos give the same. Terminal test: null. Published: Bulkowski 53-58% 'worked' with no control; vendor R1/S1 touch rates 44-84% with no distance control; Lund FX thesis (2019) rejects the traditional use. Evidence of NO effect is moderate.
concepts.engineNotes: grep finds only swing ta.pivothigh/pivotlow (709, 879). Keeping pivots out of scoring is correct; at most a display overlay (CL-6).

concepts.name: Central pivot range (CPR) and CPR-width trend-day rule
concepts.definition: BC=(H+L)/2, TC=2PP-BC, width=|2C-H-L|/3. Folklore: a narrow CPR (bottom quartile of the last 20-50 sessions) foretells a trend day, a wide one a range day; price above the CPR is bullish.
concepts.dolRole: Would set expansion and PoT scale (how far price runs) and the side bias.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T6, n=8,699 days: next-day range after a narrow CPR is 0.92 ATR vs 1.10 after a wide one; trend days 34.6% vs 37.7%. That is the opposite of the folklore. Controlling for the prior range, the coefficient sign is inconsistent (BTC +0.42 t 5.2, NDX -0.27 t -4.2). No published test exists (LuxAlgo and TradingView scripts only). CPR BC as a level is reached +4.0 pp (z 3.6, CME H24): a 'prior value' effect.
concepts.engineNotes: dayEQ (967) = CPR BC, used only as a confluence anchor (1931). The width rule is absent, which is correct.

concepts.name: Camarilla pivots
concepts.definition: H_k = C + R*m_k and L_k = C - R*m_k with m = 1.1/12, 1.1/6, 1.1/4, 1.1/2 (0.0917, 0.183, 0.275, 0.55). Folklore: fade at H3/L3; breakout through H4/L4.
concepts.dolRole: Intraday reversal and target rungs.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T1: H3 +0.6/+0.1 pp, L3 -0.3/-0.6, H4 +0.3/-1.2, L4 -1.2/-0.5 (CME/BTC, H24). Not path barriers (T8: +1.2/-1.3, ns). The vendor containment claims (70% inside H3-L3, 90% inside H4-L4) are unsourced.
concepts.engineNotes: Absent. No evidence to add them to scoring.

concepts.name: Fibonacci, Woodie and DeMark pivots
concepts.definition: Fibonacci: PP +/- 0.382/0.618/1.0 R. Woodie: PPw=(H+L+2C)/4, R1=2PPw-L, S1=2PPw-H. DeMark: X=2H+L+C if C>O, H+2L+C if C<O, H+L+2C if C=O; PP=X/4, R1=X/2-L, S1=X/2-H.
concepts.dolRole: Alternative S/R target rungs.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T1 (CME/BTC H24): FIB_R1 +0.9/-2.1, FIB_S1 -0.6/-2.3 (z -2.9 BTC), FIB_R2 -1.7/-1.1, WOOD_R1 +1.2/-1.0, DEM_H +1.0/+0.4. All within the placebo range.
concepts.engineNotes: Absent, which is correct.

concepts.name: Weekly floor pivots (PP/R1/S1 from the prior week)
concepts.definition: The floor formulas on the prior week's H/L/C (week = the symbol session's week: futures from Sunday 18:00 ET, crypto from Monday 00:00 UTC), fixed for the whole week.
concepts.dolRole: PATH BARRIER: a target lying beyond a weekly pivot is less likely to be reached. This lowers its PoT and should demote it in selection.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T8, at least one weekly pivot between price and the pool, stratified on distance x outside-PD x outside-PW x age x source: CME -6.2 pp (z -5.3), BTC -5.4 (z -6.9) at H24; -3.5 (z -6.2) and -2.0 (z -6.1) at H8. Dose-response by number crossed (BTC 0/1/2/3: +0.5/-4.2/-11.4/-14.4 pp). Confluence near the pool (T5): -6.1 (z -4.3) CME, -3.8 (z -3.9) BTC. As a level its own reach is at baseline (T2: +0.1 to +0.6). Mechanism backed by strong literature: Osler 2000 (trend interruptions at published S/R vs 10,000 random level sets) and Kavajecz & Odders-White 2004 (S/R at depth peaks).
concepts.engineNotes: Not computed. pwH/pwL already exist via f_rangeTrack (946); the prior-week close is close[1] on pwNew. Proposal CL-1.

concepts.name: Monthly pivots
concepts.definition: The floor and Camarilla formulas on the prior month's H/L/C.
concepts.dolRole: HTF S/R targets for swing traders.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T2, daily SPX/NDX 1999-2018 + BTC: M_PP -1.75 (z -3.0) at 5 days, -3.28 (z -2.8) at 20 days; M_R1 -0.25/-1.76; M_S1 -0.09/-0.91. Reached LESS often than random.
concepts.engineNotes: Absent, which is correct.

concepts.name: Naked / virgin pivots
concepts.definition: A pivot (PP or CPR) not traded during its own session. Folklore says it acts as a magnet on later sessions until touched.
concepts.dolRole: Old untouched 'unfinished business' targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T1, the prior day's PP left untouched: CME +0.8 (n 345) at H24 and -1.2 at H8; BTC -1.0. The sibling amt_profile study found naked POCs -2.3 to -4.7 pp. Null.
concepts.engineNotes: Absent, which is correct.

concepts.name: Round numbers / psychological levels (00/50/25)
concepts.definition: A grid of step S (auto: 10^floor(log10(2*daily ATR)) and the half step). Stops cluster just beyond rounds and take-profits sit at them (Osler 2003/2005).
concepts.dolRole: Where stops sit (zone depth); a barrier or 'stop short' point, not a magnet.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Literature: Osler 2003/2005, Bhattacharya-Holden-Jacobsen 2012 (strong). Own T5: a pool within 0.35 ATR of a round is swept -1.4 (CME) and -1.0 (BTC) pp less (z ~-1.6); 'at' the round -2.3 / -2.6 (z -3.3 BTC). Siblings: rounds are not magnets and sweep wicks stop short. Option-strike pinning: strong historically (Ni-Pearson-Poteshman 2005; Golez-Jackwerth 2012: at least $115m per expiry, 1992-2009), absent 2016-2025 (Elms 2026).
concepts.engineNotes: Absent. Sibling ICT-3 would add rounds as POSITIVE confluence anchors (1930-1933). T5 says the sign is negative: keep only the stop-depth part.

concepts.name: Session VWAP and deviation bands
concepts.definition: VWAP_t = sum(tp*v)/sum(v) from the session start, tp=(H+L+C)/3; sigma = sqrt(sum(v*tp^2)/sum(v) - VWAP^2); bands at +/-1 and 2 sigma. Pine: ta.vwap(src, anchor, mult).
concepts.dolRole: 'Return to value' target; 'above VWAP = buyers in control' bias.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T4 (H=8, 1h): frozen VWAP CME +1.5 (z 2.9), BTC +0.3. Moving VWAP minus moving TWAP: CME +8.5/+10.2/+10.7 pp at 0.5-1/1-2/2-4 ATR, BTC +1.1/+2.3/+4.6. Mostly mechanical (the line drifts toward price). Bands: CME about 0, BTC +/-2 sigma -1.7/-1.4 (z -4.3/-3.7). Bias (T7): no out-of-sample gain over geometry. Published: Zarattini & Aziz 2023, VWAP trend filter on QQQ (+671%, replications dispute it); about 50% of institutional flow is VWAP-benchmarked.
concepts.engineNotes: grep vwap: none. Not adding it as a target is correct: a moving target would inflate the ledger edge against the static f_potBase baseline (1314-1322).

concepts.name: Anchored VWAP (week, month, prior day, event)
concepts.definition: The VWAP sum started at a chosen anchor: week or month start, the prior day, a swing, a gap or earnings. Final prior-day VWAP = PD_VWAP.
concepts.dolRole: Dynamic S/R or 'cost basis' targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T1 (H24): W_AVWAP CME +2.3 (z 1.9), BTC -2.9 (z -3.7); M_AVWAP +0.6 / -2.8 (z -3.8); PD_VWAP +2.8 (z 2.5) CME, +1.2 BTC. Inconsistent apart from the prior-day value effect. No published backtests (Shannon, StockCharts and TrendSpider give definitions only).
concepts.engineNotes: Absent, which is correct.

concepts.name: Prior-day value levels (settlement, PP/CPR, prior-day VWAP, day mid)
concepts.definition: Levels at the prior session's centre of value: settlement / RTH close (CME ES = VWAP of 14:59:30-15:00:00 CT), PP, CPR BC/TC, PD VWAP, (PDH+PDL)/2.
concepts.dolRole: Small mean-reversion pull during the next 8-24 bars.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T1, CME H24: SETT +3.46 (z 3.7), CPR_BC +3.95 (3.6), PD_VWAP +2.76 (2.5), PP +2.34 (2.2); the same at H8. BTC: CPR_TC +1.9 (z 3.2), PP +1.5 (2.1). Placebo levels near the PP show the same effect, so it is the value location, not the formula. As confluence near a pool (T5 VALUE) it is inconclusive.
concepts.engineNotes: dayEQ (967) is a confluence anchor only; no settlement tracking. CL-4 adds a gap-gated settlement target.

concepts.name: Opening gaps / gap fill (RTH gap to the prior close)
concepts.definition: Gap = session open minus the prior session close or settlement; filled when price trades back to the prior close within the session (or N sessions). ICT NDOG/NWOG are variants.
concepts.dolRole: Prior close as a target after a gap; timing within the session.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T3 (NDX cash 2003-2018, distance-matched): gaps at least 0.5 daily ATR fill the same day 30.6% vs 22.7% (+7.9 pp, z 4.5). Pooled gap-downs of that size +12.0 (z 4.9); gap-ups about 0; small gaps +1.2 (ns). CME RTH gaps n=218: +4.5 +/- 4.8 (ns). SPX cash opens are stale (39.8% of days open = prior close). Literature: Grant, Wolf & Yu 2005 (S&P futures 1987-2002 reversals after large opening moves, strong). Vendor fill rates (77-85% for small gaps) are mostly distance.
concepts.engineNotes: Absent; sibling ICTPD-6 proposes NDOG/NWOG. CL-4 adds a gate: only gaps of at least 0.5 daily ATR.

concepts.name: Period opens (daily/midnight, weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly)
concepts.definition: The first trade of each period: futures week from Sunday 18:00 ET, crypto from Monday 00:00 UTC; month / quarter / year starts.
concepts.dolRole: Folklore: magnets and 'above the open = bullish'. Measured: weekly and monthly opens are barriers.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T2 (daily): QOPEN -1.9 (z -3.8) at 5 days and -4.1 (z -3.2) at 20 days; MOPEN -1.0 and -3.2 (z -3.0); YOPEN -0.9 and +0.7; WOPEN +1.1 and -0.6. T5: opens within 0.35 ATR of a pool -7.4 (CME, z -3.9) and -4.5 (BTC, z -4.0). T8 between price and pool: weekly open -2.1 / -3.1 (z -3.8), monthly open -7.1 (CME, z -5.4) / -0.5 (BTC). T7 and the sibling bias_dol study: no bias value beyond geometry.
concepts.engineNotes: Only intraday midnight / London / NY opens (220-222, 964-966) as positive confluence anchors (1931). Those measure neutral to negative (T5 ENG_EQOPEN: CME +0.6, BTC -2.6 / -3.3, z -3.6). CL-1 and CL-2.

concepts.name: Previous day / week high and low (PDH/PDL, PWH/PWL)
concepts.definition: The extremes of the completed prior day / week, live as pools until traded through (strict).
concepts.dolRole: Primary external liquidity targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T5 by source (1h, H24, pools vs random): CME swings -3.4, PDH -3.9, PDL -3.2, PWH -5.1, PWL -9.6; BTC -1.1, -1.5, -1.7, -1.1, -2.4. Daily T2: PDH +1.4 / PWH +2.5 at H5, a reversal-state effect after big down days. The higher tier for PW is not supported. Sibling calib_ml: external -0.27 logit.
concepts.engineNotes: 945-961 and 1790-1799 (f_rangeTrack, registry src 6/7). Tier in f_tierW (506-516) gives PW 0.92 > PD 0.80 > chart 0.25, and density adds 1.2*tier (682): not supported. Let the ledger learn the tier (CL-3).

concepts.name: Previous month / quarter / year highs and lows
concepts.definition: Extremes of the completed calendar month / quarter / year, live while untaken (strict trade-through).
concepts.dolRole: Swing-horizon external liquidity.
concepts.engineNotes: f_rangeTrack only for D and W (945-946). CL-5 (optional, Swing-mode completeness, tier at most 0.80).

concepts.name: 52-week / all-time / N-day extremes
concepts.definition: Max high / min low over 252 sessions, the full history, or 20/40/60 days (IPDA).
concepts.dolRole: Anchoring and attention points; breakout continuation at monthly horizons.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Strong for stocks at monthly horizons (George & Hwang 2004; via academic_sr). At DOL horizons, own T2: 252dH -0.2 / +0.9, 252dL 0 / -0.5, 60dH +0.4 / -0.6, 20dL +0.7 / +0.3 (5 / 20 days): baseline.
concepts.engineNotes: Absent. If sibling ACAD-5 adds them, the tier must be at most 0.80, not 0.95 / 1.0.

concepts.name: Confluence with reference anchors (engine pillar)
concepts.definition: The engine adds conf = min(1, 0.35*hits) for anchors within confATR=0.35 ATR of the zone, with weight 15/100. Anchors: aPDH, aPDL, aPWH, aPWL, dayEQ, midOpen, ldnOpen, nyOpen, htfEQ.
concepts.dolRole: Meant to raise the score of targets that coincide with key reference levels.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T5 (flagged minus unflagged, distance-bucketed, day-cluster bootstrap): engine pools as anchors CME -4.8 (z -3.6) / BTC -1.1; engine EQ / opens +0.6 / -2.6 (H8 BTC -3.3, z -3.6); weekly pivots -6.1 / -3.8; weekly / monthly opens -7.4 / -4.5; rounds -1.4 / -1.0; daily pivots +3.7 / -0.8 (inconsistent). No family is consistently positive. The sibling calib_ml regression agrees: -0.25 logit (t -2.7).
concepts.engineNotes: 139, 143, 674-680, 963-968, 1930-1933. CL-2: wConf 15 -> 0 and retune minScore about 35 -> 41; drop open / PW anchors; never add reference levels as positive anchors.

concepts.name: Above / below reference bias rules (pivot, VWAP, AVWAP, weekly / monthly open)
concepts.definition: Bullish if price is above the reference, bearish below.
concepts.dolRole: Would pick which side's liquidity is taken first.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T7 (PDH vs PDL first, both untaken): geometry-only out-of-sample accuracy 0.664 (CME, n 1,945) and 0.718 (BTC, n 3,227). Adding any sign feature leaves Brier unchanged or worse (CME: PP +0.0018 +/- 0.0011, VWAP +0.0031 +/- 0.0012, weekly AVWAP +0.0061 +/- 0.0022). The rule's 68-72% accuracy is geometry.
concepts.engineNotes: Not in the draw vector D (correct; do not add).

concepts.name: Previous settlement (official close)
concepts.definition: The exchange daily settlement (CME ES: VWAP of 14:59:30-15:00:00 CT since SER-8591, 2020; 15:14:30-15:15:00 CT before). It differs from the last trade and drives settlement-based pivots.
concepts.dolRole: Prior-value magnet and gap-fill target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: CME procedure is exchange-documented (strong for the definition). Own T1: SETT (prior 16:00 ET close) +3.46 pp (z 3.7) at H24, +3.43 (z 2.5) at H8.
concepts.engineNotes: No settlement or RTH-close tracking. CL-4.

proposals.title: Weekly-reference path barrier in score and PoT
proposals.rationale: This is the strongest and best-replicated effect in the domain. When the weekly PP/R1/S1 or the weekly open lies between price and a target, the target is reached 2-6 pp less often within 8-24 bars, about -0.25 logit per level crossed. It holds on CME and BTC, at H=8 and H=24, with z -2.6 to -7.1. It survives controls for distance, outside-prior-range, age and source, and the dose-response holds (BTC: 1 level -4 pp, 2 levels -11 pp, 3 levels -14 pp). Daily pivots and placebos show no such effect. The mechanism matches Osler 2000 and Kavajecz & Odders-White 2004. Today the engine gives full proximity credit to targets several weekly levels away.
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_SCORE): useWkBar=true; wkBarM=0.90 (score multiplier per weekly level crossed, 0.5-1.0); wkBarL=0.25 (PoT logit shift per level); wkBarMO=false (include the monthly open). State in SERIES after line 961, on the chart TF with no request.security. Declare var floats wPP, wR1, wS1, wOpn, mOpn. On pwNew (946): pwC = close[1]; wPP = (pwH + pwL + pwC)/3; wR1 = 2*wPP - pwL; wS1 = 2*wPP - pwH. On timeframe.change('W'), wOpn := open; on timeframe.change('M'), mOpn := open. Evaluate timeframe.change at global scope. Helper in STATE HELPERS (after these globals, so there are no forward references): f_xRef(px, lv, tol) counts the levels in array.from(wPP, wR1, wS1, wOpn, wkBarMO ? mOpn : na) with side 1: a > px and a <= nearEdge + tol, or side -1: a < px and a >= nearEdge - tol. It caps the count at 3. Add a Level field xRef. Scoring loop at 1939-1948, next to the f_pathVol multiplier: k = f_xRef(close, lv, confTol); lv.xRef := k; lv.mult *= math.pow(wkBarM, k). Live PoT at 2066: activePoT := min(0.95, f_sigm(f_logit(activePoT) - wkBarL * f_xRef(close, activeLv, confATR * atr))); f_logit and f_sigm exist at 484/488. Ledger: Trial gets an int field xr, set in f_openTrial (1429); f_book accumulates xbN/xbK/xbPE in 3 buckets (0, 1, 2+). Terminal Full row: 'W-REF crossed 0|1|2+: hit-base'. pBase stays the random-level baseline, so EDGE measures the benefit. Tooltip suffix: ' · across N weekly ref'. Cost: O(5) per level per confirmed bar.
proposals.risk: Tested on 1h bars only; the effect is likely smaller on 1-5 minute charts with H=30. The default 0.90 is mild, and the ledger row reveals the real effect. Weekly boundaries on exotic sessions. No weekly levels during the first week of history (na-safe).

proposals.title: Neutralise the Confluence pillar; never add reference levels as positive anchors
proposals.rationale: In own test T5, no anchor family raises sweep probability consistently. Engine pools used as anchors give -4.8 pp (CME, z -3.6); EQ and session opens are neutral to -3.3 pp (BTC H8, z -3.6). Weekly pivots (-4 to -6 pp), weekly/monthly opens (-4.5 to -7.4 pp) and round numbers (-1 to -1.4 pp), which siblings plan to add, are negative. The independent calib_ml regression also finds confluence at -0.25 logit. The pillar currently pushes selection toward pools that are less likely to be taken.
proposals.spec: Change wConf (line 143) default from 15 to 0, keeping the input and the tooltip readout. wSum (304) renormalises, and levels with conf=0 score 1.18x higher, so raise minScore (146) from 35 to about 41 to keep the selection rate; re-check the hysteresis. Remove midOpen, ldnOpen, nyOpen and aPWH/aPWL from the anchor list at 1931, or keep them for the tooltip only. Add a code comment and README note that reference levels are barriers (CL-1), not confluence. Coordinate with sibling ICT-3: do not push round levels into anchors. Optionally re-enable a signed, ledger-learned confluence through CL-3.
proposals.risk: Scores shift, so thresholds need retuning. Arrays (FVG/OB) also lose confluence credit, and that part was not tested here; the per-family f_calMult multiplier still adapts them.

proposals.title: Reference-context feature bits in the candidate (shadow) ledger
proposals.rationale: Effects are heterogeneous: the monthly open is a barrier on CME but null on BTC, and daily-pivot confluence flips sign. The engine already uses the right estimator (hits vs the random-level pBase). Per-feature lifts let each chart confirm CL-1, CL-2 and sibling claims (rounds, tier, settlement) and later feed bounded multipliers.
proposals.spec: On top of sibling CAL-3/ICT-1 (or, failing that, per-trial bits on active-target trials). Each graded candidate stores: XW = weekly references crossed (0 / 1 / 2+, from CL-1); ATW = a weekly reference within tol; ATD = a daily PP/R1/S1 within tol; ATRN = a round level (auto step 10^floor(log10(2*dailyATR)) or its half) within tol; ATV = settlement / PP / dayEQ within tol; TIER class. For each bit accumulate n, k and E = sum(pBase). Lift = ((k+2)/(E+2)) / ((K+2)/(Eall+2)), clamped to 0.8-1.2 and active when n >= 30, the same algebra as f_calMult (1376-1383). Show a Full-view table of lifts with n and CI. Optionally multiply lifts into lv.mult (off until n >= 100). State: arrays of about 18 floats.
proposals.risk: Multiple comparisons and noisy lifts on short histories. Show n and CI; default to display only.

proposals.title: Gap-gated prior-settlement target (Target: SETT) for session instruments
proposals.rationale: The prior settlement / RTH close is reached more often than random from the next open: +3.5 pp (z 3.7) on CME H24, +3.4 pp at H8. It fills well above random when the gap is at least 0.5 daily ATR: +7.9 pp (z 4.5) on NDX, mostly after gap-downs. Small gaps show no excess. Opening reversals in index futures are documented (Grant, Wolf & Yu 2005). This is the one classic level with a genuine, if small, magnet effect.
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_KEY): useSett=false; sessRTH='0930-1600'; gapMin=0.5 daily ATR; disable automatically for syminfo.type=='crypto'. Track the last close inside sessRTH with the f_sessTrack pattern (842-868). At the next RTH start, atrD = atrSlow*sqrt(86400/chartS*390/1440) and gapD = |open - sett|/atrD. If gapD >= gapMin, create a Level with new kind 8 (reference line, touch semantics), src 8, name and code 'SETT', top/bottom = sett +/- 0.05*atr, side = sign(sett - close), anchorBar = the bar that printed the settlement, qual = min(1, gapD/1.5). It expires at session end or on touch. Guard the array code paths (isArray = kind >= 2: delivIn/CE fill, origin lockout, FVG names) with kind==8 checks. Ledger: map kind 8 to a new group 4 in grp() (635) and f_grpName (543), move 'all' to index 5, resize stN/stK/stPE/stPV/stMae/stBars to 6 (1066-1071), and update the f_calMult and f_book indices.
proposals.risk: Overlaps sibling ICTPD-6 (NDOG), so build one object. On 24h futures charts it was only tested at the Globex open. The NDX evidence uses cash-index opens, and the futures sample is small.

proposals.title: Monthly high/low pools (PMH/PML) for Swing mode, tier no higher than PD
proposals.rationale: In Swing mode (W/D/4H), PDH/PWH are often already near or taken. Monthly extremes are the external liquidity swing traders watch, so this is a completeness gap users expect filled. Their measured reach is at baseline (T2: +0.3 pp at 5 days; -3.6 / +1.8 at 20 days), so the value is coverage, not edge, and the ledger will grade them.
proposals.spec: [pmNew, pmH, pmHB, pmL, pmLB] = f_rangeTrack(timeframe.change('M')) next to 945-946. Input useKeyM=false. Push to the registry like 1795-1799 with src 9 and f_tierW(9)=0.80 (not above PW). hlMult = sqrt(2592000/chartS). Names PMH/PML in f_levelName (520-521). Anchors are clamped by f_x (404). No request.security.
proposals.risk: Low: it adds candidates graded at the baseline rate, and on low-timeframe charts the anchor is clamped to 5,000 bars.

proposals.title: Optional display-only reference overlay with honest tooltips
proposals.rationale: Traders look for pivots, Camarilla and VWAP, and competitors plot them. Showing the weekly references used by CL-1 explains why a target was demoted, without adding them to scoring.
proposals.spec: clsShow input: Off / Weekly Refs / Weekly + Daily Pivots (G_DISP, default Off). On barstate.islast, draw dotted lines from each period's first bar to xR with tiny right labels W-PP, W-R1, W-S1, W-O (and PP/R1/S1). Recycle them through the existing dLn/dLb arrays, at most 8 lines and 8 labels, in the theme's dim colours. Never shown in Clean style unless the user picks it. Tooltip: 'Weekly reference: measured as a barrier for targets beyond it, not a magnet.'
proposals.risk: Clutter, which off-by-default and the drawing cap contain.

result.summary: SMT divergence is not a reversal signal. Across 4 asset classes, 3 timeframes and several parameter sets (my CME event study, n≈48k sweeps), a sweep where the comparison symbol fails to take its twin reverses in a 1-ATR race 50.5% of the time vs 50.8% for joint sweeps. The day-cluster CI of the difference is [-2.2,+1.5] pp. Neither killzones (NY AM SMT 44.3% vs joint 48.4%), PDH/PDL key levels, PSP or divergence magnitude rescue the claim. Three independent public studies agree: an ES/NQ event study with 11k-141k rows found 49.5-51.8% win rates; an NQ/ES/YM/RTY 2018-26 analysis ran 88 tests with none beyond chance (47-51% of 1σ races); and an audited ES/NQ SMT+FVG system produced -0.10 to -0.17R expectancy over n≈600 trades. What SMT does predict is that the laggard catches up. When the sister takes its twin while the chart's matching pool is intact, that pool is hit within H bars more often than a distance- and momentum-matched intact pool: lift 1.075 [1.057,1.092], or 1.054 [1.033,1.077] with the 1-bar delay a non-repainting Pine feed imposes. Pools more than 1 ATR away show a lift of 1.06-1.18 (Δlogit +0.15 to +0.30). A placebo with the comparison symbol shifted 500 bars gives a null 1.017, and the effect holds in index, metals, FX and crypto on 5m, 15m and 1h. Syncs are front-loaded: 20-22% happen on the next bar, about 50% within 6 bars and 69-73% within 30; the median is 5 bars intraday. The engine's existing raid-close classification (L1578-1582) separates the next-liquidity side by 11-15 pp, while SMT adds at most 3 pp, so SMT should not feed D or the raid classification by default. The recommended optional module costs one request.security call ([1] offset, lookahead_on, chart TF, time-aligned with time[1]; 7 of 40 requests). It assigns each liquidity pool a twin on the comparison symbol and tracks it with a state machine (intact / sister-swept / chart-led SMT). It handles inverse pairs (DXY) by sign-normalising, and switches off when the 100-bar |correlation| drops below 0.5. Sister-swept pools get a bounded score multiplier and a PoT logit shift that decay with a half-life of about 8 bars. A small sister ledger calibrates the boost live against the engine's own f_potBase random-level baseline and also shows users whether the ICT reversal reading holds on their chart. Evidence quality: Firecrawl credits ran out and most hosts were blocked, so web sources are search summaries plus cloned GitHub repos; the quantitative core is my own reproducible study under study/smt_tools.

concepts.name: SMT divergence (two-symbol swing SMT, chart leads)
concepts.definition: Chart A forms a pivot high at bar T (pivot length L, usable at T+L). Twin R_B = max(high_B[T-w..T+w]) with w = 0-2 bars, and it must be intact at T+L. A sweeps when high_A > P (strict trade-through). It is an SMT when B has not traded above R_B by the decision bar (optionally after a grace period). Lows mirror this. GXV-style range variant: XOR(A took its previous-interval extreme, B took its own), with intervals matched by exact open and close times.
concepts.dolRole: Practitioners read it as proof that the sweep was a stop run, so they expect a reversal toward the opposite liquidity, i.e. a flip of the draw side.
concepts.evidenceNotes: The evidence is AGAINST a reversal edge. My study: 1-ATR race 50.5% (SMT) vs 50.8% (joint), n=16,258/16,187, diff CI [-2.2,+1.5] pp; with Pine timing 49.7% vs 50.7%, CI [-2.8,+0.7]. thomas-quant/mss-research ES/NQ: 49.5-51.8% win rates on n=11k-141k. Genjutsu Kai 2018-26: 88 tests, 47-51%, none beyond chance. charisjv19 ES/NQ system: E=-0.10 to -0.17R, PF 0.75-0.85, n≈600. Sources: github.com/thomas-quant/mss-research, github.com/unclehk2000/genjutsu-kai, github.com/charisjv19/intermarket-divergence-scanner.
concepts.engineNotes: No second-symbol feed: every request uses syminfo.tickerid (L923-925, L939, L981-982). The sweep handler L1575-1590 classifies raids by the chart's close only. Given the evidence, this omission costs nothing for reversal prediction.

concepts.name: Sister sync / laggard catch-up (sick sister)
concepts.definition: B trades through its twin while A's matching pool is still intact. A is the laggard (sis=2). Sync = A later takes its pool; hold = it never does within the window. Sync odds per Genjutsu Kai: logistic recalibration of 2Φ(-gap/(κσ√t_left)).
concepts.dolRole: It picks WHICH pool is the draw: the laggard's untaken twin has a higher probability of touch than its distance alone implies, a continuation cue. Timing: hazard of about 23%, 14%, 12% on the next bars; median 5 bars intraday.
concepts.evidenceNotes: My study, with a distance × momentum matched control: lift 1.075 [1.057,1.092] with no delay and 1.054 [1.033,1.077] with Pine's 1-bar delay. Pools >1 ATR away: 1.10 [1.07,1.14] (Δlogit +0.17). Placebo with B shifted 500 bars: 1.017 [0.986,1.047]. Holds in index, metals, FX and crypto, and on 5m, 15m and 1h. Own-pool-before-opposite-pool race 70.9% vs 67.0%. Genjutsu Kai sync-odds model: AUC 0.85, calibrated within 6 pp on a locked 2025-26 test; 53-64% of 30m SMTs held.
concepts.engineNotes: Level (L318-347) and Ext (L363-371) have no twin or state fields. evaluate() (L661-697), f_potModel (L1303-1312) and the live PoT (L2066-2067) cannot use the cue.

concepts.name: Inverse-correlation SMT (DXY vs EURUSD/GBPUSD)
concepts.definition: Mirror B with high_B' = -low_B and low_B' = -high_B, then apply the positive-correlation logic unchanged. Sign chosen manually or by rolling correlation sign (Auto). DXY = 50.14348112 × EURUSD^-0.576 × USDJPY^0.136 × GBPUSD^-0.119 × USDCAD^0.091 × USDSEK^0.042 × USDCHF^0.036.
concepts.dolRole: Lets FX charts use DXY as the sister. EUR is 57.6% of DXY, so GBPUSD or USDCHF carry more independent information.
concepts.evidenceNotes: DXY weights are from ICE's USDX brochure (strong). EURUSD-DXY ρ ≈ -0.97 (Forex.com) and -0.915 to -0.93 on daily returns from other vendors (weak-moderate). Nothing here shows predictive value beyond the general SMT findings.
concepts.engineNotes: Not present. Proposal: sign-normalise the B feed once, latch the sign, and reset twins when the sign re-latches.

concepts.name: Correlation regime gate
concepts.definition: ρ = ta.correlation(log-return A, log-return B, 100) on time-aligned bars. SMT is live only when |ρ| ≥ 0.5; a negative ρ means the pair is inverse in Auto mode.
concepts.dolRole: Stops spurious sister states when the pair decouples (correlation drift, roll artefacts, bad data).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Measured ρ (5m/15m/1h): ES-NQ 0.96/0.96/0.97; ES-YM 0.91/0.92/0.90; NQ-YM 0.81-0.82 (1h rolling p10 0.37); GC-SI 0.78-0.80 intraday; 6E-6B 0.86-0.90; MBT-MET 0.82-0.90. The GC/SI 1h dataset is about 0.1 through 2025, which looks like a data problem; it shows why a gate is needed. Practitioners say SMT 'means less when correlation drifts'.
concepts.engineNotes: Not present.

concepts.name: Raid-close classification (hold = continuation, reject = reversal)
concepts.definition: On a liquidity sweep: close beyond the zone top means hold (continuation, +1); close back inside the level means reject (reversal, -1). Accumulated by tier into liqEvt with a half-life.
concepts.dolRole: Primary sweep-reversal vs continuation signal feeding the draw vector D.
concepts.evidenceNotes: My data: share of sweeps where the opposite pool is taken before the next pool beyond: reject 44.9-45.6% vs hold 30.1-31.5% (L3 H12); 41.8-43.8% vs 30.0-31.5% (L5 H30). Part of this is geometric. SMT minus joint within each class stays within about ±3 pp, so SMT adds nothing beyond this classification.
concepts.engineNotes: L1578-1582 (evt by close vs lv.top/lv.price), decay at L1535, wL=0.30 in D at L1894. Keep it, and do not let SMT override it.

concepts.name: SMT at key levels (PDH/PDL, sessions, HTF) and in killzones
concepts.definition: The same SMT test applied to the previous-day, session or HTF extremes, with B's own range extremes as twins, optionally restricted to London or NY AM killzones.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed to make the reversal read reliable at higher-timeframe liquidity.
concepts.evidenceNotes: PDH/PDL, 922 events: 1-ATR reversal SMT 44.0% vs joint 44.8% (CI [-15,+14]). The 2-ATR race shows SMT reversing LESS (41.6% vs 59.2% at g=0; 46.1% vs 52.7% at g=3). Killzones, 1-ATR reversal SMT vs joint: NY AM 44.3% vs 48.4% (CI [-8.6,+0.1]); London 51.0% vs 48.4% (CI [-1.2,+6.7]).
concepts.engineNotes: Key ranges come from f_rangeTrack (L815-840) and f_sessTrack (L843-867) on chart data only; f_kzAff (L596-601) has no SMT interaction. Only the sync use of these twins is recommended.

concepts.name: PSP (precision swing point, candle-colour divergence)
concepts.definition: At a swing or sweep bar, the correlated assets' candles close in opposite directions (e.g. ES closes up, NQ closes down at the high). Optional pin-bar filter; implementations differ on how a doji counts.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed one-candle reversal confirmation.
concepts.evidenceNotes: My data: 1-ATR race 50.4% (PSP) vs 49.8% (no PSP), n=6,039/41,481, CI [-1.4,+2.7] pp. Within SMT events: 49.8% vs 49.6%.
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended.

concepts.name: Triad SMT (one vs two sisters)
concepts.definition: Three correlated indices (ES/NQ/YM). Track whether one or both sisters have taken their twins while the chart's pool is intact.
concepts.dolRole: Stronger version of the laggard cue.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Lift with one sister 1.046 [1.010,1.081] (n=4,286); with both 1.062 [1.018,1.108] (n=1,757). The CIs overlap, so the second sister's increment is not significant.
concepts.engineNotes: Optional later; it needs a second request.

concepts.name: Sync timing / lead-lag hazard
concepts.definition: After B leads, record the number of bars until A trades through its twin, and its hazard by bar.
concepts.dolRole: Answers WHEN: an ETA for a laggard target, and the decay constant for any boost.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Within ≤1/≤6/≤12/≤30 bars: 5m 21/49/61/73%, 15m 22/51/61/73%, 1h 20/44/54/69%; never within 300 bars 9-11%; median given sync 5 bars (5m/15m) and 7 bars (1h). Genjutsu Kai: 11-20% in the first minute, about half that in the second. Academic lead-lag exists only at ms-to-second scale (Dobrev & Schaumburg 2018).
concepts.engineNotes: The engine has an ETA from ttHit/dHit (L1067-1070) for DOL hits, but no cross-asset timing.

concepts.name: Relative strength / leader-laggard designation
concepts.definition: The symbol that took its liquidity first is the 'leader'. Folk rule: trade the strongest index for longs and the weakest for shorts, and treat the laggard's failure as weakness.
concepts.dolRole: Would choose whose liquidity is the draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No quantitative support found. My laggard result contradicts the 'weakness → failure' reading: the laggard's twin is MORE likely to be hit than a matched control.
concepts.engineNotes: Covered better by the sister-sync state.

concepts.name: Continuous divergence magnitude (lag size)
concepts.definition: (A overshoot beyond P in A-ATR) minus (B overshoot beyond R_B in B-ATR) at the decision bar; Genjutsu-style minimum lag of k×σ of the return spread.
concepts.dolRole: Would grade SMT strength.
concepts.evidenceNotes: 1-ATR race is flat across quintiles of the divergence (50.2-51.3%). Genjutsu: the minimum-lag filter 'removes clutter; it is not an edge filter'.
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended beyond a de-clutter threshold for marks.

concepts.name: Dow-theory confirmation / pairs convergence (background)
concepts.definition: Correlated averages must confirm each other's highs (Dow). Matched pairs whose normalised prices diverge by more than 2σ tend to re-converge (pairs trading).
concepts.dolRole: Theoretical basis: divergences tend to close. The data says closure via the laggard (continuation) is more likely than chance at sweep time.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Brown, Goetzmann & Kumar 1998 (JF 53:1311-1333): Hamilton's Dow timing produced positive risk-adjusted returns 1902-1929; the confirmation rule is not isolated. Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst 2006 (RFS 19:797-827): up to ~11% annualised excess returns from pairs convergence 1962-2002 (daily horizon, stocks). Neither tests intraday SMT directly.
concepts.engineNotes: Context only.

proposals.title: Optional correlated-symbol feed, twin levels and sister state machine
proposals.rationale: The infrastructure for every evidence-backed intermarket feature. It gives each liquidity pool a time- or interval-matched twin on the comparison symbol and tracks whether the sister or the chart takes it first. One request, non-repainting, off by default.
proposals.spec:
Inputs (new G_SMT group): smtOn=false; smtSymIn=input.symbol('') with an auto pair via a switch on syminfo.root (ES↔NQ, YM/RTY→ES, MES↔MNQ, GC↔SI) and str.replace for crypto BTC↔ETH and FX EURUSD↔GBPUSD; smtCorr Auto/Positive/Inverse; smtRhoMin=0.5; smtW=2.
Feed (SERIES, after L982): [bOr,bHr,bLr,bCr,bTr] = request.security(smtReq ? smtSym : syminfo.tickerid, timeframe.period, [open[1],high[1],low[1],close[1],time[1]], lookahead=barmerge.lookahead_on, ignore_invalid_symbol=true); bAl = bTr == time[1].
Correlation: rho = ta.correlation(rA, rB, 100) on aligned log returns (na is ignored). Latch the sign; smtLive = bAl and |rho| ≥ smtRhoMin. Normalise for inverse pairs: bHn = sign<0 ? -bLr : bHr, bLn = sign<0 ? -bHr : bLr.
Types: add float twin=na, int sis=0 (0 untracked, 1 intact, 2 sister-swept, 3 chart-led SMT) and int sisBar=na to Level (L318-347) and Ext (L363-371). Defaults keep the positional Ext.new at L1224 valid.
Twins: f_twinState(b0,b1,hi) (STATE HELPERS after L1209) loops k over [b0,b1] with bHn[bar_index-k-1], capped at 450 bars, then checks (b1, bar_index-1] for an earlier sister sweep. Windows: chart swings [anchor±w] at L1761/L1773; STF/HTF pivots [a-w, a+r-1+w] with r=round(f_tfRatio(tf)) at L1783-1789; PDH/PDL, PWH/PWL and sessions from lag-correct trackers f_rangeLag(inPrev, emit, bHn, bLn) that fold the [1]-shifted B bar into the old period before emitting. Extend f_pushExt with (tw, st, sb); on a merge, f_mergeAt keeps the outermost twin; registry re-entry (L1846-1851) copies twin/sis/sisBar.
Update (new step 3a before L1557, and in step 4): if smtLive and sis==1 and (side==1 ? bHn>twin : bLn<twin), set sis:=2 and sisBar:=bar_index-1. When the sign re-latches, set sis:=0 everywhere.
Chart-led sweep (L1578): if sis==1, push a pending record and resolve it on the next confirmed bar (B's sweep-bar data has then arrived): synced = joint, otherwise SMT. This one-bar deferral keeps it non-repainting.
proposals.risk: Auto-pair strings can be wrong for some data feeds (shown as 'SMT: no data'; user can override). Session mismatches freeze the state. Contract-roll gaps on non-adjusted continuous symbols can fake sister sweeps (mitigation: the correlation gate, back-adjusted symbols). The 450-bar twin loops run only at level birth.

proposals.title: Sister-swept (laggard) pools: bounded score multiplier and PoT logit shift
proposals.rationale: The only intermarket effect that survived controls. A pool whose twin the sister already took is hit more often than a distance- and momentum-matched pool: lift 1.054 [1.033,1.077] with Pine timing, and 1.10 [1.07,1.14] (Δlogit +0.17) beyond 1 ATR. The placebo is null at 1.017. This is target-specific: it picks which same-side pool is the draw.
proposals.spec:
Score (step 17, L1938-1948, next to f_kzAff and f_calMult): if smtOn and smtMode != 'Display only' and lv.isLiquidity() and lv.sis==2, then dk = 0.5^((bar_index-lv.sisBar)/smtHL) with smtHL default 8 (sync hazard), fa = clamp((dATR-0.5)/1.0, 0, 1), and lv.mult *= 1 + (f_sisLift()-1)*dk*fa.
PoT (after L2067): pb = ledger mean baseline (default 0.4); dl = f_logit(min(0.99, f_sisLift()*pb)) - f_logit(pb); activePoT = min(0.95, f_sigm(f_logit(activePoT) + dl*dk*fa)), using the existing f_logit/f_sigm at L484/L488.
f_sisLift() = clamp((K+20*1.06)/(E+20), 0.90, 1.25) from smt-ledger (prior 1.06 worth 20 expected hits).
No change to D. Optionally add int sis to Trial so the DOL hit rate can be split by sister state.
proposals.risk: Modest effect size; it can be swamped by other pillars, which is acceptable. The distance ramp avoids double counting with proximity. A bad data pair can produce false states, mitigated by the correlation gate.

proposals.title: Live sister ledger: sync lift vs f_potBase, plus SMT-vs-joint reversal race
proposals.rationale: Makes the intermarket claims measurable on the user's own chart and pair, consistent with the engine's random-baseline accuracy philosophy. It calibrates smt-sync-boost and gates the optional ICT reversal reading.
proposals.spec:
Sync records: when any pool or registry entry turns sis=2 with 0<d≤maxATR, push SisT{side, edge=nearEdge, bar0, pBase=f_potBase(d, side)}, at most 64 open. Each confirmed bar: if hit (side==1 ? high>edge : low<edge), K+=1, E+=pBase, n+=1; if bar_index-bar0≥H, E+=pBase, n+=1.
Race records: each resolved chart-led sweep of a tracked pool (SMT or joint) starts a 1-ATR race from the decision close; book reversal-first wins and n per arm.
Storage: var array<float> smtSt(8). Place the helpers after f_book (~L1500), since they call f_potBase (L1314). Use the 2H-block cluster variance from f_book (L1463-1469) for z-scores.
Panel: 'SYNC ×1.07 (n 212, z 2.1) · SMT-REV 49% (n 120) vs JOINT 51% (n 180)'.
proposals.risk: Small n on higher timeframes, hence the shrinkage prior. Records overlap and share price paths, hence the clustered variance.

proposals.title: Keep SMT out of the draw vector and raid classification; ledger-gated ICT reversal option
proposals.rationale: Prevents a popular but unsupported rule from degrading D. Evidence: SMT minus joint 1-ATR race CI [-2.8,+0.7] pp with Pine timing; no killzone, key-level or class rescue; three external studies at 47-52% or with negative expectancy. The engine's raid-close classification already separates the next-liquidity side by 11-15 pp.
proposals.spec:
smtMode options: 'Sync' (default), 'Reversal (ledger-gated)', 'Display only'.
In Sync mode, a chart-led SMT does not touch liqEvt (L1579-1582) or D (L1892-1895).
In 'Reversal (ledger-gated)' mode: only when the smt-ledger race shows SMT-REV minus JOINT-REV > 0 with z ≥ 2 and n ≥ 50 per arm, add evt = -side*tier*0.5 to liqEvt at the pending-sweep resolution. Otherwise show 'ICT reversal: not supported on this chart (z=…)'.
proposals.risk: Users expect 'SMT = reversal'. The tooltip and panel must explain why in one line.

proposals.title: SMT alerts, Clean label tag and Terminal rows
proposals.rationale: Surfaces the actionable intermarket events (sister took liquidity and the chart lags; SMT at sweep) without cluttering the Clean look.
proposals.spec:
Two new alertconditions after L2093, plus alert() messages at bar close: 'SMT · Sister Took Liquidity' (a draw-side or active pool turns sis=2; message includes sync odds and ETA) and 'SMT · Divergence at Sweep' (pending sweep resolved as SMT; message includes ledger reversal rates).
Clean style: suffix '· SMT↻' on the DOL label when activeLv.sis==2, with a tooltip line. No extra table rows.
Terminal style: row 'SMT  NQ1! ρ .96  ▲LAG BSL 1.2ATR · ETA 5b' and an accuracy row from smt-ledger.
Optional marks: dashed line from the swept pivot to the sweep extreme, labelled SMT/↻, at most 12 in a FIFO like f_ghost (L1253).
proposals.risk: Clutter and drawing caps (500 lines and labels). Marks are off by default in Clean.

proposals.title: Sync ETA and boost decay learned from the live sync hazard
proposals.rationale: Answers WHEN for laggard targets. Measured: 20-22% sync on the next bar, about 50% within 6 bars, median 5 bars intraday and 7 bars on 1h.
proposals.spec: Record the bars from sisBar to the chart's sweep for synced pools in an array capped at 300 (like ttHit, L1067). ETA = median, with a prior of 5 bars intraday or 7 bars on 1h when n < 30. Set the smt-sync-boost half-life to max(3, median) once n ≥ 30. Show 'sync ETA ~5b' in the HUD and tooltip.
proposals.risk: Minimal: right-censoring biases the ETA short, which matters little for an indicative readout.

proposals.title: Exact interval matching for key-range twins (PDH/PDL, PWH/PWL, sessions)
proposals.rationale: Pairs with different trading hours (FX vs DXY, crypto vs CME) can misalign day or session ranges. Exact open/close interval matching (GXV-style) keeps the highest-tier pools' sister states correct. There is no new signal: PDH/PDL SMT shows no reversal edge.
proposals.spec: Optional toggle. Add B's daily time and time_close to the smt-core tuple (still one request), or compare session flags. Only emit a B range twin when B's interval boundaries equal the chart's; otherwise leave the twin as na (sis=0). Reuses f_rangeLag from smt-core.
proposals.risk: Extra complexity for a minority of pairs.

proposals.title: Optional second sister (triad ES/NQ/YM)
proposals.rationale: With two sisters, 'fully lagging' pools (both sisters took their twins) show lift 1.062 [1.018,1.108] vs 1.046 [1.010,1.081] for one sister. The increment is not significant, so this is worth adding only if a user's ledger confirms the single-sister effect.
proposals.spec: A second input.symbol and one more request (8 of 40). Per Level, add twin2 and sis2. The boost uses max(lift1, lift2) when one sister has swept, and caps the combined lift at 1.15 when both have. Track it in the same ledger with a 'both' bucket.
proposals.risk: More state and complexity for a marginal gain.

concepts.name: Trading day / day boundary per asset class
concepts.definition: CME futures 18:00->17:00 ET, with Sunday 18:00 opening Monday's trading day and a daily halt 17:00-18:00. Spot FX and metals 17:00->17:00 New York, with the week from Sunday 17:00 to Friday 17:00. Crypto 00:00->24:00 UTC, 7 days. US stocks: RTH 09:30-16:00, ETH 04:00-20:00. Pine: timeframe.change("D") and time_tradingday follow the exchange trading day.
concepts.dolRole: Defines which extremes are PDH/PDL/PWH/PWL and when they are emitted. A different boundary gives different targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: BTC: UTC-day vs NY-midnight-day high differs on 45.7% of days and low on 42.7% (n≈2927) [this study]. Pine docs on time_tradingday.
concepts.engineNotes: Lines 945-946 use the exchange day via timeframe.change; there is no per-asset choice (sibling SESS-6). On stock ETH charts the day starts at 04:00.

concepts.name: RTH vs ETH key levels (PDH/PDL, prior RTH close, RTH open)
concepts.definition: ETH levels are the full-session extremes. RTH levels are the extremes of 09:30-16:15 ET for CME index futures (named session "us_regular") or 09:30-16:00 for stocks (session.regular). Prior RTH close is the gap reference; the RTH open is an anchor.
concepts.dolRole: Different, widely watched liquidity sets. AMT and stock traders target RTH levels; ICT futures traders target ETH levels.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Index futures: ETH high outside RTH 45.8% of days, low 50.0%; either extreme 70-85%; median gap 0.19-0.28 ADR (n=216). Next-day take: ES RTH PDH 58.5% vs ETH 50.9% [this study rth_eth.py].
concepts.engineNotes: Uses the chart session only (945, 952-961, 1790-1799). No RTH H/L on ETH futures charts. Stock ETH charts produce a pre/post-market PDH. nyOpen at 966 is a confluence anchor only.

concepts.name: DST-correct session clock (local exchange time)
concepts.dolRole: Puts the Asia/London range pools, opens and killzones where activity actually happens, which drives when session liquidity is run.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Index futures 04:00 vs 03:00 bucket: winter 21%, mismatch 93%, summer 46% of days (log-ratio +0.35, CI 0.24-0.46). Gold 21:00 bump +0.11 winter vs +0.55 mismatch. Asia range differs on 68-87% of US-winter days (n=81-87). Ito & Hashimoto 2006 tie activity to local market hours.
concepts.engineNotes: A single tz input (219) for all windows (107-109, 220-226, 799, 836, 948-950, 964-966, 971-974). Asia misses the Tokyo first hour from Nov to Mar; London is off by 1 h for about 4 weeks a year.

concepts.name: Sessions and killzones on 24/7 and RTH-only assets
concepts.definition: Crypto: weekday-only killzones, because weekend volume is 13-16% of the total. Stocks: no Asia/London sessions; the active windows are 09:30-11:00 and 15:00-16:00. Session strings default to all 7 days.
concepts.dolRole: Avoids weekend noise pools and wrong hysteresis states; enables an asset-appropriate timing context.
concepts.evidenceNotes: BTC weekday 13-20 UTC share 35.3% -> 43.7% (2017-19 -> 2023-25) [this study]. Kaiko: weekend share 28% (2019) -> 13-16% (2024); US hours 46% of 2024 volume through April.
concepts.engineNotes: Killzones (971-976) and session trackers fire on crypto weekends. On stocks, 10:00-13:30 is OFF-KZ with hysteresis x kzHx (976), and Asia/London never fire.

concepts.name: Midnight open availability per asset
concepts.definition: The ICT New York midnight open exists for futures, FX and crypto, but not for stocks (no bars at 00:00) or on charts whose bars do not open in 00:00-01:00. Stock substitutes are the 09:30 RTH open and the 04:00 pre-market open.
concepts.dolRole: Confluence anchor and possible target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Definitional.
concepts.engineNotes: f_sessOpen (798-803) returns na and the anchor silently drops from confluence (1931). There is no substitute.

concepts.name: Session-open gaps (weekend, daily halt, overnight on RTH charts, holidays)
concepts.definition: A gap bar is one where time - time[1] > 2 x chart seconds. A gap-through is open beyond a level on that bar. It jumps over resting stops rather than running them.
concepts.dolRole: Determines whether a removed pool was 'taken' by a run, and whether the raid outcome should feed the draw vector D.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Mechanism-level. Siblings found no fill magnet beyond distance for weekend gaps (session_stats §2.9).
concepts.engineNotes: Sweep loop 1556-1585 and registry raid 1587-1592 treat a gap-through as a sweep and add evt to liqEvt (1580-1582). f_step (1434) already settles gaps at the open, so the ledger is correct.

concepts.name: FX rollover window artefact (17:00 New York)
concepts.definition: Around 17:00 NY, bank liquidity is thin, CME FX futures are halted 17:00-18:00, and spreads widen (e.g. 0.5 -> 18 pips). Bid-based charts print wicks that never traded at mid.
concepts.dolRole: False sweeps of pools near price, and fake reversal raids, every trading day on spot FX and metals.
concepts.evidenceNotes: EURUSD 1-h 2017-18: 17:00 NY median wick fraction 0.70 vs 0.51-0.61 for all other hours, at range 0.56 and tick volume 0.77 of the daily mean [this study fx.py]. CME 'When FX futures pause' (2026) and broker FAQs.
concepts.engineNotes: No rollover handling. Wick hits delete the pool and push liqEvt.

concepts.name: Continuous-futures roll gap and back-adjustment
concepts.definition: On a contract switch the unadjusted continuous series jumps by the inter-contract spread. TradingView back-adjustment is off by default; it shifts older data by the close difference at the switch.
concepts.dolRole: The roll jump sweeps every pool in its path, creates fake FVGs and displacement, and shifts the real liquidity of old levels by the basis.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ES 2025-12-14 Sunday open +56.5 pts = 6.2x the median 1-h range; contract flips on ES 2025-09-03 and on GC/CL [this study sanity.py]. TradingView support 43000685266. ESZ23 -> ESH24 +51 pts example.
concepts.engineNotes: No detection. Pine offers ticker.modify(..., backadjustment=on/off) and syminfo.current_contract.

concepts.name: Holidays, half days and outages
concepts.definition: CME halts at 12:00 CT on holidays and resumes at 17:00 CT for the next trade date. Black Friday and Christmas Eve close early, and so do Monday holidays. Exceptional outages also occur (CME Globex 2025-11-28, about 10 h).
concepts.dolRole: A short session's extremes are weak previous-day liquidity and distort bar-count conversions.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Short sessions' median range/ADR: ES 0.76, NQ 0.65, GC 0.58 vs about 1.0; Thanksgiving 0.08 ADR (n=11 ES/NQ) [this study]. Russell: Black Friday volume about 45%, Christmas Eve about 20% of normal.
concepts.engineNotes: Short-day extremes are pushed as full PDH/PDL with tier 0.80 (1790-1794, 506-515).

concepts.name: Bars per period on session-limited assets
concepts.definition: Measured chart bars per trading day or week, not wall-clock seconds. On a 5-min chart: stocks have 78 RTH bars/day vs 288 assumed; futures have about 1380 bars/week vs 2016.
concepts.dolRole: Freshness (ageing) of PD, PW and HTF levels on their own clock.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Arithmetic.
concepts.engineNotes: f_tfRatio (567-568), hmD 1792 and hmW 1797 use in_seconds/chartS, so stock PD/PW/HTF freshness runs 1.9-2.3x too slow.

concepts.name: Scheduled macro releases by asset (08:30, 10:00, FOMC 14:00, EIA Wed 10:30, ECB, fixes)
concepts.definition: Releases come on a known calendar. US data at 08:30 ET, with Thursday claims every week and NFP usually on the first Friday. EIA crude every Wednesday at 10:30. FOMC 8 times a year at 14:00 ET. ECB at 14:15 CET. WM/R fix at 16:00 London. LBMA gold at 10:30 and 15:00 London.
concepts.dolRole: Predicts WHEN pools near price are run, and by how much, per asset. Release-bar raids carry little directional information.
concepts.evidenceNotes:
This study: Thursday 08:00-hour ratio ES 1.33 vs Monday 1.02, NQ 1.36 vs 1.07, GC 1.75 vs 1.27 (n≈50-56). FOMC 14:00 bar: ES 2.7x, NQ 2.3x, GC 4.9x, CL 1.3x (n=8). EIA effect inconclusive in 2025-26. Literature:
- Ederington & Lee 1993: adjustment in the first minute, about 15 min of elevated volatility, later moves unrelated to the first minute.
- Fleming & Remolona 1999: spreads widen at the release.
- ABDV 2003: jumps tied to surprises.
- Evans 2018: WM/R fix volatility and reversal.
concepts.engineNotes: No event awareness anywhere. Sibling TIME-7 proposes one manual event.

concepts.name: Pre-announcement drift (macro and FOMC)
concepts.definition: Some releases drift in the correct direction from about 30 minutes before (40-50% of the adjustment). Equities drifted up about 49 bp in the 24 h before FOMC (1994-2011).
concepts.dolRole: Draw-direction tilt into an event.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Kurov et al. 2019 JFQA: 9-11 of 20-21 releases. Lucca & Moench 2015: +49 bp; 'puzzling' post-2011.
concepts.engineNotes: Not modelled. It is small and decaying, so at most ledger-gated.

concepts.name: Session-directional drifts (overnight drift at the Europe open, FX own-hours depreciation, gold night effect)
concepts.definition: Documented return patterns by session: S&P futures +3.6% annualised at 02:00-03:00 ET (1998-2019); currencies weaken during their own trading hours; COMEX gold overnight returns positive and day returns negative.
concepts.dolRole: Would bias D by time of day.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Boyarchenko et al. RFS 2023, but flat in 2021-25 (NY Fed 2026). Breedon & Ranaldo JMCB 2013. Springer gold study.
concepts.engineNotes: Deliberately not modelled. Not recommended as fixed priors.

concepts.name: Crypto weekend compression and weekend range
concepts.definition: Saturday and Sunday (UTC) ranges are compressed by the calendar. The weekend high/low (Sat 00:00 to Mon 00:00 UTC) is a pool for Monday.
concepts.dolRole: A high-probability Monday target. Weekend PD levels and killzones are noise.
concepts.evidenceNotes: BTC Saturday range 0.83 -> 0.46 ADR and Sunday 0.86 -> 0.72 (2017-19 -> 2023-25). Monday takes the weekend range 81.7% (n=416) vs 66.3% for weekday two-day ranges; +9 to +12 pp within near-side distance bins [this study crypto.py].
concepts.engineNotes: Not tracked. On Monday, PDH/PDL = Sunday's thin range.

concepts.name: Crypto funding times
concepts.definition: Binance perps settle funding at 00:00/08:00/16:00 UTC, and switch to 4-hourly or hourly when the rate is capped.
concepts.dolRole: Possible timing anchor.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Funding-hour bars 1.05-1.12 vs neighbours 0.98-1.02, confounded with the 00 UTC day open and the 08 UTC London open [this study].
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended.

concepts.name: Volume availability by asset
concepts.definition: Cash indices have no volume (syminfo.volumetype "n/a"); FX has tick volume; crypto has base or quote volume.
concepts.dolRole: Validity of the LVN and path-volume features.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Definitional.
concepts.engineNotes: VP features are silently inert when volume is 0 (guards at 2252 and 1420); there is no user notice.

concepts.name: Settlement-as-close for futures daily bars
concepts.definition: TradingView uses the settlement price as the D close by default; the intraday bars show the last trade.
concepts.dolRole: Body-break structure on D uses settlement closes.
concepts.evidenceNotes: TradingView support 43000685268; Pine ticker.modify settlement_as_close.
concepts.engineNotes: Consistent with what users see on D charts. Documentation note only.

concepts.name: Structural market changes 2025-26
concepts.definition:
Changes that alter day definitions and session sets:
- CME crypto futures 24/7 since 2026-06-01, so no new CME gaps.
- NYSE 22-hour trading approved; Nasdaq 24/5 targeted for H2 2026.
- TradingView offers a '24h' session for some US stocks.
concepts.dolRole: Day definitions and session sets change over time.
concepts.evidenceNotes: CME press release 2026-06-01; Cooley/Bloomberg; TradingView support.
concepts.engineNotes: Handle through detection (syminfo.session, syminfo.type), not constants.

concepts.name: Daily/weekly chart gating of key levels
concepts.definition: PDH/PDL are meaningful only below D; PWH/PWL only below W.
concepts.dolRole: Prevents mislabelled targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Definitional: timeframe.change("D") is true on every W bar.
concepts.engineNotes: On a W chart 'PDH' = the prior week's high (945, 1790-1794), de-duplicated against PWH.

proposals.title: Market profile: auto-detect the asset class and apply per-asset session/level presets
proposals.rationale: All asset-specific behaviour needs one switch. Today, futures-style New York sessions run on stocks (where Asia, London and midnight never fire) and on crypto weekends (where they fire on noise). The engine reads no syminfo fields at all.
proposals.risk: Exotic symbols (CFD indices, spot commodities typed 'commodity' or 'spot') may be misclassified. 'Other' is the safe fallback and manual override exists. Historical ledger numbers change per profile.

proposals.title: DST-correct session clock: Asia follows Tokyo (Shanghai for metals), London follows Frankfurt; New York-time inputs kept
proposals.rationale: Activity follows local clocks. In the mismatch weeks the European-open spike sits at 04:00 ET on 93% of days, and the London-open anchor at 02:00 ET lands an hour before Frankfurt. The Asia range differs on 68-87% of US-winter days. The fix is cheap and the ledger can A/B it.
proposals.spec:
Input sessClock = 'Local (DST-correct)' | 'New York fixed (ICT)'.

f_offMin(zone) = (hour(time,zone)*60 + minute(time,zone)) - (hour(time,NY)*60 + minute(time,NY)), wrapped to (-720, 720].
- Asia shift = 780 - f_offMin('Asia/Tokyo'). For metals use 720 - f_offMin('Asia/Shanghai'), where isMetal = GC/MGC/SI/SIL roots or XAU/XAG base currency. In US winter the shift is -60.
- London shift = 360 - f_offMin('Europe/Berlin'). It is +60 in the mismatch weeks and 0 otherwise.
- Apply the shifts to the parsed New York-time session minutes, then test membership with TIME-3's minute-of-day overlap test f_inWin(sM+sh, eM+sh).
- Fallback without TIME-3: build the 'HHmm-HHmm' session string at runtime (zero-pad by hand) and call time(timeframe.period, sessStr, 'America/New_York'). The session argument is a series string.

Applies to f_sessTrack (948-949), f_sessOpen (965) and the Asia/London killzones (971-972). NY windows and the midnight open are unchanged.
proposals.risk: ICT users expect fixed New York times, so that option is kept. Toggling changes winter Asia levels and the ledger history. Four extra hour()/minute() calls per bar: negligible.

proposals.title: RTH and ETH key levels from named sessions (RTH H/L, prior RTH close, RTH open)
proposals.rationale: On index futures at least one ETH extreme differs from RTH on 70-85% of days (median 0.2 ADR). RTH levels are what AMT and stock traders watch. The engine only has chart-session PDH/PDL, and stock ETH charts produce a pre/post-market 'PDH'. A per-family ledger can grade the two sets.
proposals.spec:
Input keySess = Auto | Chart | RTH | Both (G_KEY). Auto = Both for index futures, RTH for stocks, Chart for the rest.

Ticker: rthTk = futures ? ticker.new(syminfo.prefix, syminfo.ticker, "us_regular") : ticker.modify(syminfo.tickerid, session.regular). A missing named session falls back to the default (docs).

Request: [rH, rL, rC, rT] = request.security(rthTk, f_tfSafe("D"), [high[1], low[1], close[1], time[1]], lookahead = barmerge.lookahead_on). This is one extra request and non-repainting.

On f_changedT(rT), push src 8 'RTH H/L' (tier 0.78; add it to f_tierW 505-516, f_levelName 518-529 and the comment at 316) with anchor bar f_anchorScan(rH, true, anchorMax). f_pushExt de-duplicates equal prices.

RTH mode on stock ETH charts replaces the chart PD push (1790-1794). Add rC (prior RTH close) and the RTH open (session.isfirstbar_regular for stocks; the 09:30 window open for futures) to the anchors at 1931. Clean codes 'RTH H'/'RTH L'.
proposals.risk: Non-US futures use other session names (e.g. xetr_regular) and fall back to ETH, which is handled by de-dup. On a 1H chart the 09:30 anchor is approximate. RTH PDH updates at the next trading-day start (18:00) through the [1] mapping, not at 16:15.

proposals.title: Session-artefact guard: rollover wicks and session-open gaps are not raids
proposals.rationale: On spot FX and metals, 17:00 NY rollover wicks are spread artefacts (median wick fraction 0.70 vs 0.51-0.61; CME shows a 0.5 -> 18 pip widening). Session-open gaps jump stops rather than run them. Today both delete pools and inject raid events into D, and rollover wicks inflate DOL HIT%.
proposals.spec:
State:
- gapBar = barstate.isconfirmed and (time - time[1]) > 2*chartS*1000;
- rollWin = mkt == FX and bar in '1655-1715' New York (TIME-3 overlap on coarse bars).

Sweep loop (1556-1585):
1. In rollWin, liquidity needs a CLOSE beyond the level. Wick-only touches increment lv.tests (density) and the level stays.
2. On gapBar with open beyond the level, remove the level and ghost it as '⤳ GAPPED', with evt = 0 (no liqEvt contribution).

The same two rules apply to the registry raid check (1587-1592). f_step (1434): rollover-window wicks are not hits for liquidity targets; add t.gapHit for the accuracy panel ('of which gapped').

Measure: artefact-hit counts per 1000 bars; EDGE z before vs after.
proposals.risk: A genuine rollover-hour run that closes back inside is ignored as a sweep, though still recorded as a test. Mid-based feeds lose a little sensitivity.

proposals.title: Continuous-futures roll handler: detect the switch bar and shift stored levels by the jump
proposals.rationale: With back-adjustment off (the TradingView default), every quarterly (index) or monthly (CL) roll jump (+56.5 pts on ES Dec-2025, 6.2x the median hourly range) sweeps pools, creates fake FVGs and displacement, and offsets all old levels by the basis.
proposals.risk: Two extra requests. The coefficient uses daily closes near the switch, so it approximates the intraday jump. Contract flips in thin sessions produce paired opposite jumps, which are handled. Must be verified on ES1! in TradingView.

proposals.title: Crypto weekend model: weekend range as a Monday target, weekend state for killzones and PD levels
proposals.rationale: BTC weekend ranges are calendar-compressed (Saturday 0.46 ADR in 2023-25). Monday takes them 81.7% of the time, +9 to +12 pp above weekday ranges at the same distance. Weekend volume share is 13-16%. The engine runs killzones and sessions on weekends, and uses Sunday's thin range as Monday's PDH/PDL.
proposals.risk: Part of the Monday excess may come from the low weekend ATR. The ledger's random-level baseline controls for that. A choice of day convention is needed for NY-anchored users.

proposals.title: Session completeness: measured bars per day/week and short-day (holiday) handling
proposals.rationale: Holiday, half-day and outage sessions (median 0.58-0.76 ADR, Thanksgiving 0.08) become full PDH/PDL with tier 0.80. Wall-clock bars-per-day makes PD/PW/HTF freshness 1.9-2.3x too slow on stocks (78 vs 288 bars/day on 5m) and about 1.2x on futures/FX weekly.
proposals.risk: f_tfRatio becomes series-valued (callers already treat it as series float). There is an na warm-up on the first day (fallback to wall clock). The holiday evidence is small-n.

proposals.title: Asset-aware scheduled-event calendar: recurring presets plus a FOMC/date list, news flag, news-window rules and a ledger split
proposals.rationale: Liquidity runs cluster at known times, and by asset: Thursday 08:30 lifts the ES 08:00 hour 1.33x vs 1.02x; FOMC 14:00 runs 4.9x on gold but 1.3x on crude. Release-minute direction carries little information (Ederington-Lee), and some releases drift about 30 min early (Kurov et al.). This extends TIME-7's single manual event.
proposals.risk: User-maintained date lists go stale (empty default = no-op). The NFP rule is approximate. Variance multipliers are defaults until learned.

proposals.title: Data-availability and chart-timeframe guards
proposals.rationale: Volume-profile features are silently inert on no-volume symbols (cash indices). A W chart mislabels the prior week's high as PDH. Cash-index opening prints are stale. Tick volume and 24h stock sessions are not flagged.
proposals.spec:
- If syminfo.volumetype == "n/a": force needVP false (979); the panel shows 'VOL n/a' with an LVN tooltip suggesting the futures contract.
- If 'tick': the panel shows 'VOL tick'.
- syminfo.type == "index": HUD note 'cash index: open print stale; gaps unreliable'.
- useKeyD effective only when timeframe.in_seconds() < 86400; useKeyW only when < 604800 (gating at 1790/1795).
- syminfo.session not regular/extended: show 'SESSION 24h'.
- Optional input settleAsClose for D structure via ticker.modify(..., settlement_as_close = settlement_as_close.off); default inherit.
proposals.risk: None material.
